akhfash:15-15.t: He said ﴿بِأَيْدِي سَفَرَةٍ﴾: their singular is "السافِر", like "الكافِر" and "الكَفَرة".

akhfash:16-16.t: And He said ﴿كِرَامٍ بَرَرَةٍ﴾: their singular is "البارّ", and "البَرَرة" is a plural (in the meaning) of "الأَبْرار".

akhfash:17-17.t: And He said ﴿قُتِلَ ٱلإِنسَانُ مَآ أَكْفَرَهُ﴾: its meaning is on two aspects: some said "as an exclamation of wonder (taʿajjub)", and some said: "what thing has made him disbelieve?" (أيُّ شَيْءٍ أَكْفَرَهُ).

akhfash:20-20.t: He said ﴿ثُمَّ ٱلسَّبِيلَ يَسَّرَهُ﴾: you say "الطريقَ هَدَاهُ" ("the road — He guided him"), that is: "He guided him to the road" (هداهُ الطريقَ).

celaleyn:1-1.t: ﴿عَبَسَ﴾ the Prophet: his face grimaced, ﴿وَتَوَلَّى﴾ turned away, because

celaleyn:2-2.t: ﴿أَنْ جَاءَهُ الْأَعْمَى﴾ ʿAbd Allāh ibn Umm Maktūm, and interrupted him in what he was occupied with: someone whose Islam he hoped for, of the nobles of Quraysh, whose Islam he was eager for. The blind man did not know that he was occupied with that, so he called out to him: "Teach me some of what Allah has taught you." The Prophet ﷺ went off to his house, and he was reproached for that by what was revealed in this sura. After that, whenever he came, he would say to him: "Welcome to the one on whose account my Lord reproached me," and would spread out his cloak for him.

celaleyn:3-3.t: ﴿وَمَا يُدْرِيكَ﴾ lets you know ﴿لَعَلَّهُ يَزَّكَّى﴾ in it the tāʾ of the underlying form is assimilated into the zāy; i.e. he might purify himself of sins through what he hears from you,

celaleyn:4-4.t: ﴿أَوْ يَذَّكَّرُ﴾ in it the tāʾ of the underlying form is assimilated into the dhāl; i.e. take admonition, ﴿فَتَنْفَعَهُ الذِّكْرَى﴾ the admonition heard from you; in one reading with the accusative [تَنْفَعَهُ], as the answer to the expression of hope (tarajjī).

celaleyn:6-6.t: ﴿فَأَنْتَ لَهُ تَصَدَّى﴾ — in one reading with doubling of the ṣād, by assimilation of the second tāʾ of the underlying form into it — you turn to him and attend to him,

celaleyn:8-8.t: ﴿وَأَمَّا مَنْ جَاءَكَ يَسْعَى﴾ a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of جَاءَ,

celaleyn:9-9.t: ﴿وَهُوَ يَخْشَى﴾ Allah; a ḥāl from the fāʿil of يَسْعَى; and he is the blind man,

celaleyn:10-10.t: ﴿فَأَنْتَ عَنْهُ تَلَهَّى﴾ in it the other tāʾ of the underlying form is dropped; i.e. you busy yourself away from him.

celaleyn:11-11.t: ﴿كَلَّا﴾ do not do the like of that! ﴿إِنَّهَا﴾ i.e. the sura, or the ayahs, ﴿تَذْكِرَةٌ﴾ an admonition for creation;

celaleyn:12-12.t: ﴿فَمَنْ شَاءَ ذَكَرَهُ﴾ memorised that and took admonition from it,

celaleyn:13-13.t: ﴿فِي صُحُفٍ﴾ a second khabar (predicate) of إِنَّهَا, and what precedes it is a parenthesis (iʿtirāḍ); ﴿مُكَرَّمَةٍ﴾ with Allah,

celaleyn:14-14.t: ﴿مَرْفُوعَةٍ﴾ in the heaven ﴿مُطَهَّرَةٍ﴾ kept clean from the touch of devils,

celaleyn:15-15.t: ﴿بِأَيْدِي سَفَرَةٍ﴾ scribes who copy it from the Preserved Tablet,

celaleyn:16-16.t: ﴿كِرَامٍ بَرَرَةٍ﴾ obedient to Allah the Exalted, and they are the angels.

celaleyn:17-17.t: ﴿قُتِلَ الْإِنْسَانُ﴾ cursed is the unbeliever; ﴿مَا أَكْفَرَهُ﴾ a question of rebuke, i.e. what led him to unbelief?

celaleyn:18-18.t: ﴿مِنْ أَيِّ شَيْءٍ خَلَقَهُ﴾ a question of affirmation (taqrīr); then He explained it, saying:

celaleyn:19-19.t: ﴿مِنْ نُطْفَةٍ خَلَقَهُ فَقَدَّرَهُ﴾ a clinging clot, then a chewed lump, to the end of his creation;

celaleyn:20-20.t: ﴿ثُمَّ السَّبِيلَ﴾ i.e. the way of his coming out of his mother's belly ﴿يَسَّرَهُ﴾

celaleyn:21-21.t: ﴿ثُمَّ أَمَاتَهُ فَأَقْبَرَهُ﴾ placed him in a grave that covers him;

celaleyn:22-22.t: ﴿ثُمَّ إِذَا شَاءَ أَنْشَرَهُ﴾ for the resurrection.

celaleyn:23-23.t: ﴿كَلَّا﴾ truly ﴿لَمَّا يَقْضِ﴾ he has not done ﴿مَا أَمَرَهُ﴾ his Lord with.

celaleyn:24-24.t: ﴿فَلْيَنْظُرِ الْإِنْسَانُ﴾ a look of taking heed ﴿إِلَى طَعَامِهِ﴾ how it was decreed and arranged for him:

celaleyn:27-27.t: ﴿فَأَنْبَتْنَا فِيهَا حَبًّا﴾ such as wheat and barley,

celaleyn:29-29.t: ﴿وَزَيْتُونًا وَنَخْلًا﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here]

celaleyn:31-31.t: ﴿وَفَاكِهَةً وَأَبًّا﴾ what beasts graze on; it is also said: straw,

celaleyn:32-32.t: ﴿مَتَاعًا﴾ as a provision or as providing, as preceded in the sura before it, ﴿لَكُمْ وَلِأَنْعَامِكُمْ﴾ also preceded in it.

celaleyn:34-34.t: ﴿يَوْمَ يَفِرُّ الْمَرْءُ مِنْ أَخِيهِ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here]

celaleyn:35-35.t: ﴿وَأُمِّهِ وَأَبِيهِ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here]

celaleyn:36-36.t: ﴿وَصَاحِبَتِهِ﴾ his wife ﴿وَبَنِيهِ﴾ يَوْمَ is a badal (substitute) for إِذَا, and its answer (jawāb) is indicated by:

celaleyn:37-37.t: ﴿لِكُلِّ امْرِئٍ مِنْهُمْ يَوْمَئِذٍ شَأْنٌ يُغْنِيهِ﴾ a state that occupies him from the affairs of others; i.e. each one is occupied with himself.

celaleyn:39-39.t: ﴿ضَاحِكَةٌ مُسْتَبْشِرَةٌ﴾ joyful; and that is the believers.

celaleyn:42-42.t: ﴿أُولَئِكَ﴾ the people of this state ﴿هُمُ الْكَفَرَةُ الْفَجَرَةُ﴾ i.e. those who combine unbelief and wickedness.

daas-irab:1-4.t: ﴿عَبَسَ﴾: a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya) and has no grammatical position. ﴿وَتَوَلَّى﴾: a past verb whose agent is latent; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿أَنْ﴾: a maṣdar-forming particle that puts the verb in the accusative; ﴿جاءَهُ﴾: a past verb and its object; ﴿الْأَعْمى﴾: postponed agent; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from an and the verb is accusative by removal of the preposition. ﴿وَما يُدْرِيكَ﴾: an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject), and an imperfect verb and its first object, the agent being latent; ﴿لَعَلَّهُ﴾: لعل and its noun; ﴿يَزَّكَّى﴾: an imperfect verb whose agent is latent; the verbal clause is the khabar (predicate) of لعل, the clause لعل… is the second object of يدريك, the clause يدريك… is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ ما, and the clause ما يدريك is resumptive. ﴿أَوْ﴾: a conjunction; ﴿يَذَّكَّرُ﴾: conjoined to يزكي. ﴿فَتَنْفَعَهُ﴾: the fāʾ is causal (sababiyya), and an imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb) by an implied an after the causal fāʾ; the hāʾ is mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿الذِّكْرى﴾: agent.

daas-irab:5-10.t: ﴿أَمَّا﴾: a particle of condition and detailing; ﴿مَنِ﴾: a relative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿اسْتَغْنى﴾: a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of من. ﴿فَأَنْتَ﴾: the fāʾ is the linking fāʾ (rābiṭa) and ﴿أنت﴾ is mubtadaʾ; ﴿لَهُ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) what follows them; ﴿تَصَدَّى﴾: an imperfect verb whose agent is latent; the clause is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ أنت, the clause أنت… is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ من, and the clause من… is resumptive. ﴿وَما﴾: the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya) and ﴿ما﴾ is negative; ﴿عَلَيْكَ﴾: fronted khabar; ﴿أن﴾: a maṣdar-forming particle that puts the verb in the accusative; ﴿لا﴾: negative; ﴿يَزَّكَّى﴾: an imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb) by an, its agent latent; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from an and the verb is the postponed mubtadaʾ, and the nominal clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿وَأَمَّا﴾: a particle of condition and detailing; ﴿مَنْ﴾: mubtadaʾ; ﴿جاءَكَ﴾: a past verb and its object, the agent being latent; the clause is the ṣila of من; ﴿يَسْعى﴾: an imperfect verb whose agent is latent; the clause is a ḥāl, and the clause أما من… is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَهُوَ﴾: the wāw is circumstantial and ﴿هُوَ﴾ is mubtadaʾ; ﴿يَخْشى﴾: an imperfect verb whose agent is latent; the verbal clause is the khabar and the nominal clause is a ḥāl. ﴿فَأَنْتَ عَنْهُ تَلَهَّى﴾: parsed like فأنت له تصدى.

daas-irab:11-16.t: ﴿كَلَّا﴾: a particle of deterrence and rebuke; ﴿إِنَّها﴾: inna and its noun; ﴿تَذْكِرَةٌ﴾: its khabar (predicate); the clause is resumptive. ﴿فَمَنْ﴾: the fāʾ is a resumptive particle and ﴿من﴾ is a conditional noun that puts the verb in the jussive, mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿شاءَ﴾: a past verb in the position of a jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir); ﴿ذَكَرَهُ﴾: a past verb in the position of a jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); the hāʾ is mafʿūl bihi (direct object) and the agent is latent; the clause is the apodosis and has no grammatical position, the two clauses of the condition and the apodosis are the khabar of the mubtadaʾ من, and the clause من… is resumptive. ﴿فِي صُحُفٍ﴾: naʿt (adjective) of تذكرة; ﴿مُكَرَّمَةٍ﴾: adjective of صحف; ﴿مَرْفُوعَةٍ مُطَهَّرَةٍ﴾: two adjectives of صحف; ﴿بِأَيْدِي﴾: also an adjective of صحف; ﴿سَفَرَةٍ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); ﴿كِرامٍ بَرَرَةٍ﴾: two adjectives of an omitted qualified noun, its implied form being "ملائكة" (angels).

daas-irab:17-23.t: ﴿قُتِلَ﴾: a passive past verb; ﴿الْإِنْسانُ﴾: nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position. ﴿ما﴾: a complete indefinite (nakira tāmma), mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿أَكْفَرَهُ﴾: a past verb and its object, the fāʿil (agent) being latent (mustatir); the verbal clause is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ, and the nominal clause is resumptive. ﴿مِنْ أَيِّ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb after them; ﴿شَيْءٍ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); ﴿خَلَقَهُ﴾: a past verb and its object, the agent being latent; the clause is resumptive. ﴿مِنْ نُطْفَةٍ﴾: attached to what follows them; ﴿خَلَقَهُ﴾: a past verb and its object, the agent being latent; the clause is a badal (substitute) for the preceding one; ﴿فَقَدَّرَهُ﴾: conjoined to خلقه by the fāʾ. ﴿ثُمَّ﴾: a conjunction; ﴿السَّبِيلَ﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an omitted verb explained by the one mentioned after it; ﴿يَسَّرَهُ﴾: an imperfect verb [Translator's note: so in the source; يسّر is a past verb] and its object, the agent being latent; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿ثُمَّ أَماتَهُ فَأَقْبَرَهُ﴾: conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿ثُمَّ﴾: a conjunction; ﴿إِذا﴾: a conditional adverb that does not put the verb in the jussive; ﴿شاءَ﴾: a past verb whose agent is latent; the clause is in the position of a genitive by annexation (iḍāfa); ﴿أَنْشَرَهُ﴾: a past verb and its object, the agent being latent; the clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) and has no grammatical position. ﴿كَلَّا﴾: a particle of deterrence and rebuke; ﴿لَمَّا يَقْضِ﴾: an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by لما, the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the weak letter from its end, the agent being latent; ﴿ما﴾: direct object; ﴿أَمَرَهُ﴾: a past verb and its object, the agent being latent; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of ما, and the clause كلا… is resumptive and has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:24-26.t: ﴿فَلْيَنْظُرِ﴾: the fāʾ is a resumptive particle, and an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by the lām of command; ﴿الْإِنْسانُ﴾: fāʿil (agent); ﴿إِلى طَعامِهِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; the clause is resumptive. ﴿أَنَّا صَبَبْنَا﴾: anna and its noun, and a past verb and its agent; ﴿الْماءَ﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿صَبًّا﴾: mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); the clause is the khabar (predicate) of anna, and the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from anna and what follows it is a badal of inclusion (badal ishtimāl, a substitute) for طعامه. ﴿ثُمَّ﴾: a conjunction; ﴿شَقَقْنَا الْأَرْضَ شَقًّا﴾: conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:27-32.t: ﴿فَأَنْبَتْنا﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); ﴿فِيها﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; ﴿حَبًّا﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَعِنَباً وَقَضْباً وَزَيْتُوناً وَنَخْلًا﴾: conjoined to what precedes them. ﴿وَحَدائِقَ﴾: also conjoined; ﴿غُلْباً﴾: naʿt (adjective) of حدائق. ﴿وَفاكِهَةً وَأَبًّا﴾: conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿مَتاعاً﴾: mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), accusative (manṣūb); ﴿لَكُمْ﴾: attached to متاعا; ﴿وَلِأَنْعامِكُمْ﴾: conjoined to what precedes them.

daas-irab:33-37.t: ﴿فَإِذا﴾: the fāʾ is a resumptive particle and ﴿إذا﴾ is a conditional adverb that does not put the verb in the jussive; ﴿جاءَتِ الصَّاخَّةُ﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is in the position of a genitive by annexation (iḍāfa). ﴿يَوْمَ﴾: an adverb of time, badal (substitute) for إذا; ﴿يَفِرُّ الْمَرْءُ﴾: an imperfect verb and its agent; the clause is in the position of a genitive by annexation; ﴿مِنْ أَخِيهِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) what precedes them; ﴿وَأُمِّهِ وَأَبِيهِ﴾: conjoined to what precedes them; ﴿وَصاحِبَتِهِ وَبَنِيهِ﴾: also conjoined. ﴿لِكُلِّ﴾: attached to an omitted fronted khabar (predicate); ﴿امْرِئٍ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); ﴿مِنْهُمْ﴾: naʿt (adjective) of امرئ; ﴿يَوْمَئِذٍ﴾: an adverb of time annexed to one like it; ﴿شَأْنٌ﴾: postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿يُغْنِيهِ﴾: an imperfect verb and its object, the agent being latent (mustatir); the verbal clause is an adjective of شأن, and the nominal clause لكل امرئ… is resumptive and has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:38-42.t: ﴿وُجُوهٌ﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿يَوْمَئِذٍ﴾: an adverb of time annexed to one like it; ﴿مُسْفِرَةٌ﴾: khabar (predicate); ﴿ضاحِكَةٌ مُسْتَبْشِرَةٌ﴾: two further predicates of وجوه; the nominal clause is resumptive. ﴿وَوُجُوهٌ﴾: mubtadaʾ; ﴿يَوْمَئِذٍ﴾: an adverb of time annexed to one like it; ﴿عَلَيْها﴾: fronted khabar; ﴿غَبَرَةٌ﴾: postponed mubtadaʾ; the clause is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, and the clause وجوه… is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿تَرْهَقُها﴾: an imperfect verb and its object; ﴿قَتَرَةٌ﴾: fāʿil (agent); the verbal clause is a second khabar of وجوه. ﴿أُولئِكَ﴾: mubtadaʾ; ﴿هُمُ﴾: a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl); ﴿الْكَفَرَةُ الْفَجَرَةُ﴾: two predicates; the clause is resumptive.

dervis-irab:18-42.t:
* Vocabulary:
(غُلْباً) plural of أغلب, like حمر as the plural of أحمر and حمراء. One says: حديقة غلباء, i.e. a garden of thick trees, with its plots densely intertwined. So the gardens are ones with thick trees; it is a majāz mursal (metonymic trope), like المرسن (an animal's nose-place, used for a human nose), in the sense of "thick" in general. There is also a figurative usage in the attribution (isnād), because the gardens themselves are not thick; rather, their trees are thick. Al-Zamakhsharī's wording is:
"It may be that each garden is made غلباء, meaning their density and the abundance and size of their trees, as you say: 'a huge garden'; or that its trees are made غلب, i.e. huge and thick. The original use of the description غلب is for necks, and it was then borrowed. ʿAmr ibn Maʿdīkarib said:
يمشي بها غلب الرقاب كأنهم ... بزل كسّين من الكحيل جلالا
(Thick-necked ones walk in it, as though they were nine-year-old camels clothed in tar as caparisons.)"
One says أسد أغلب, i.e. a lion with a thick neck; القلب [Translator's note: so in the source; presumably الغلب] is its plural; it was then borrowed for anything thick. البزل is the plural of بازل, used for male and female camels when the tooth has broken through, which happens in the ninth year; الكحيل is tar; and الجلال is the plural of جلّ (a caparison). He is describing a desert in which thick-necked lions walk, as though they were young camels smeared with tar until it lay upon them like caparisons. So كسين is an explicit metaphor (istiʿāra muṣarraḥa) and الجلال is a tarshīḥ (a reinforcing detail of the metaphor). It is also narrated as كأنهم, by borrowing the pronoun of rational beings for others.
In al-Asās and al-Lisān, the gist is: "بينهما غلاب, i.e. a contest for mastery between them; تغالبوا على البلد (they contended for the land); غلبته على الشيء: I took it from him, and he is مغلوب عليه (overpowered for it). أيغلب أحدكم أن يصاحب الناس معروفا means: is any of you unable…? 'He is a free man and he has refused — shall we then overpower him against himself?', i.e. shall we compel him? شاعر مغلّب: one who was often overcome, or one who was judged the victor — so it is both blame and praise. Imruʾ al-Qays said:
فإنك لم يفخر عليك كعاجز ... ضعيف ولم يغلبك مغلّب
(No weak, helpless man has boasted over you, nor has one often overcome overcome you.)
Among the figurative usages: هضبة غلباء (a massive hill), عزة غلباء (overpowering might), اغلولب العشب (the grass grew thick), and حدائق غلبا."
(أَبًّا) In al-Miṣbāḥ: "الأبّ is the pasture which people have not sown, of what beasts and grazing livestock eat." It seems to be taken from أبّه when one heads for it, because it is sought out and travelled to for grazing, or from أبّ لكذا when one gets ready for something, because it is ready for grazing. Al-Zamakhsharī's wording: "الأب is pasture, because it is يؤبّ, i.e. sought and travelled to for grazing; الأب and الأم are brothers [in meaning]. He said:
جذمنا قيس ونجد دارنا ... ولنا الأبّ به والمكرع
(Our root is Qays, Najd is our home, and ours in it are the pasture and the watering-place.)"
الجذم, with kasra and sometimes fatḥa, is the root from which something else is cut off. الأب and الأم, with fatḥa and doubling, mean pasture, because it is يؤبّ and يؤمّ, i.e. sought out. المكرع is the watering-place. He says: we are of the tribe of Qays, Najd is our home, and ours in it, i.e. in Najd, are the pasture and the place of drinking; it contains self-praise for nobility and courage.
It has been said that the Companions — who were the people of the Hijaz and the owners of the language in which the Qur'an was revealed — did not understand some of the rare words in the verses of the Book. Of this is what Abū ʿUbayd reported in al-Faḍāʾil from Ibrāhīm al-Taymī: that Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq was asked about the saying of the Exalted «وفاكهة وأبا» and said: "What sky would shade me and what earth would carry me if I said about the Book of Allah what I do not know?" It is transmitted from Anas that ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb recited on the pulpit «وفاكهة وأبا» and said: "This fruit we know; so what is الأب?" Then he turned back upon himself and said: "This, indeed, is affectation, O ʿUmar." In one narration: then he threw down a staff that was in his hand and said: "This, by the life of Allah, is affectation; and what harm is it to you, O son of ʿUmar's mother, not to know what الأبّ is?" Then he said: "Follow what has become clear to you of this Book, and what has not, leave it." Al-Zamakhsharī commented on ʿUmar's words with an excellent comment, which we cite below:
"If you say: this resembles a prohibition of pursuing the meanings of the Qur'an and investigating its difficulties, I say: he did not mean that. Rather, those people's greatest concern was devoted to action, and occupying oneself with any knowledge that is not acted upon was affectation in their view. He meant that the verse is set out to remind man of the favour of his food and to call forth his gratitude, and it is known from the purport of the verse that الأب is part of what Allah has caused to grow for man as provision for him and his livestock. So hold to what is more important: rising to give thanks to Allah for what has become clear to you and was not obscure of the favours He enumerated, and do not let yourself be distracted from it by seeking the meaning of الأبّ and knowing the particular plant of which it is the name. Be content with the general knowledge until it becomes clear to you at another time. Then he advised people to proceed on this course in similar difficulties of the Qur'an."
How did the exegesis of the Qur'an begin?
To complete this important discussion, we see fit to present this subject in some detail because of its full connection with the method we have followed in this book. The fact is that the Qur'an occupied many groups of people for a period of time: the people of faith were occupied with it, and the people of disbelief pursued it, each from the angle of his concern. Qur'anic studies and exegesis first began in the time of the Messenger ﷺ. In his era we see a Bedouin asking him about the meaning of some words of the Qur'an, as in the saying of the Exalted «ولم يلبسوا إيمانهم بظلم», saying: "And which of us has not wronged himself?" The Prophet ﷺ explained it as shirk (associating partners with Allah) and cited as evidence for it the saying of the Exalted: «إن الشرك لظلم عظيم». Many ḥadīths connected with the exegesis of the Qur'an are narrated from the Prophet ﷺ in the books of ḥadīth such as al-Bukhārī, Muslim and others; some of them are limited to mentioning its merits and explaining some of its verses with a brief explanation that shows the legislative point or the admonition in the verse. It is narrated from Abū Hurayra that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "There will come on the Day of Resurrection a huge, fat man who will not weigh with Allah as much as the wing of a gnat. Recite, if you wish: فلا نقيم لهم يوم القيامة وزنا." However, not everything that has come in ḥadīth on exegesis may be given consideration. Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal — in the third century AH — says: "Three things have no basis: exegesis, the battle-prophecies (al-malāḥim) and the campaigns (al-maghāzī)." Perhaps he meant the exegesis in which people mixed sound and unsound ḥadīth, which was the subject of give-and-take and of many people's statements in his age.
Moreover, the Companions took two positions in early Islam. Some were scrupulous about speaking on the Qur'an; among them were Abū Bakr, ʿUmar, ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar and others, and ʿAbd Allāh used to reproach Ibn ʿAbbās for interpreting the Qur'an by poetry. The second group were those who were not scrupulous and interpreted the Qur'an according to what they understood from the Messenger, or according to their own understanding by comparison with Arabic poetry and the speech of the Arabs. Among them were ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās and those who took from them. Ibn ʿAbbās stood at the head of the exegetes by opinion who took the poetry of the Arabs as a means of uncovering the meanings of the Qur'an, and ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib used to praise Ibn ʿAbbās and say: "It is as though he looks at the unseen through a thin veil."
In al-Mubarrad's al-Kāmil and Abū al-Faraj al-Iṣfahānī's al-Aghānī: ʿUmar ibn Abī Rabīʿa, while a youth, came in to Ibn ʿAbbās, who had with him Nāfiʿ ibn al-Arzaq [Translator's note: the source has الأرزق here and الأزرق below; the name is Nāfiʿ ibn al-Azraq]. Ibn ʿAbbās said to him: "Will you not recite to us something of your poetry, O son of my brother?" So he recited to him:
أمن آل نعم أنت غاد فمبكر ... غداة غد أوم رائح فمهجر
(Is it from the family of Nuʿm that you are setting out early tomorrow morning, or going in the evening, or at midday?) [Translator's note: أوم in the source is presumably أم.]
until he completed it — and it is eighty verses. Al-Azraq said to him: "By Allah, Ibn ʿAbbās! We drive the camels hard to come to you and ask you about religion, and a youth of Quraysh comes to you reciting folly to you and you listen to him?" He said: "By Allah, I did not hear folly." He said: "Did he not recite to you:
رأت رجلا أما إذا الشمس عارضت ... فيخزى وأما بالعشي فيخسر
(She saw a man who, when the sun faces him, is disgraced, and in the evening is ruined)?"
He said: "That is not what he said. He only said: فيضحى وأما بالعشي فيخصر (he is exposed to the sun, and in the evening he is cold)." He said: "Do you memorize what he said?" He said: "By Allah, I have heard it only this very hour." Then he recited it from its beginning to its end. It was said to him: "We have never seen anyone with a better memory for transmission than you." He said: "I have never heard anything and forgotten it; and I hear the voice of the wailing woman and block my ears, disliking to memorize what she says." Then it happened that Nāfiʿ asked Ibn ʿAbbās about the saying of the Exalted «لا تظمأ فيها ولا تضحى». He said: "You will not sweat in it from the intensity of the sun's heat." He said: "And do the Arabs know that?" He said: "Yes. Have you not heard the poet's word فيضحى?" Among the Companions who followed this approach were Ibn Masʿūd, Ubayy ibn Kaʿb and others, and they were followed by al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī, Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, Mujāhid, ʿIkrima, Qatāda, al-Suddī and others.
(الصَّاخَّةُ) In al-Mukhtār: "الصاخة is the cry that deafens by its intensity. You say صخ الصوت, of the pattern ردّ; and from it the Resurrection was named الصاخة." Al-Zamakhsharī said: "صخ لحديثه is like أصاخ له (he listened attentively to it); so the Blast was described as الصاخة figuratively, because people listen attentively to it." Abū Bakr ibn al-ʿArabī said: "الصاخة is that which bequeaths deafness, while it makes one hear; and this is of the marvels of eloquence, like his saying:
أصمّهم سرّهم أيام فرقتهم ... فهل سمعتم بسر يورث الصمما
(Their secret deafened them in the days of their parting — have you ever heard of a secret that bequeaths deafness?)
and the saying of Abū Tammām:
أصم بك الناعي وإن كان اسمعا ... وأصبح مغنى الجود بعدك بلقعا
(The announcer of your death deafened [us] with you, though he made [us] hear; and the abode of generosity after you has become a barren waste.)"
By the life of Allah, the cry of the Resurrection makes one hear: it deafens to this world and makes one hear the matters of the Hereafter.
(تَرْهَقُها) In al-Mukhtār: "رهقه: it covered him, of the pattern طرب; and from it is the saying of the Exalted: ولا يرهق وجوههم قتر ولا ذلّة; and in the ḥadīth: 'When one of you prays towards something, let him يرهقه,' i.e. let him come close to it and not be far from it."
(قَتَرَةٌ) a blackness like smoke; you see nothing more dreadful than the combination of dust and blackness on the face.

* I'rab:
(مِنْ أَيِّ شَيْءٍ خَلَقَهُ مِنْ نُطْفَةٍ خَلَقَهُ فَقَدَّرَهُ) a resumptive clause set out to begin explaining what He bestowed on him, after the emphatic description of him as ungrateful for the favours of his Creator. (من أيّ شيء) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) (خلقه). The interrogative is for affirmation (taqrīr) together with belittlement; some exegetes combined the two and said: "Here the interrogative is for affirming the belittlement." (من نطفة) is a badal (substitute) with repetition of the preposition from his saying (من أي شيء خلقه). The fāʾ is for sequence in mention, and (قدّره) is a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) a latent (mustatir) pronoun, optionally, its implied form being "huwa", and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
(ثُمَّ السَّبِيلَ يَسَّرَهُ ثُمَّ أَماتَهُ فَأَقْبَرَهُ ثُمَّ إِذا شاءَ أَنْشَرَهُ) (ثم) is a conjunction for sequence with delay. (السبيل) is accusative by ishtighāl (preoccupation of the verb) with an implied verb, its implied form being "ثم يسّر السبيل يسّره"; the definiteness conveys generality. The clause (يسّره) is explicative. Al-Samīn's wording: "His saying ثم السبيل يسّره: the pronoun may refer to man, with السبيل an adverb, i.e. He made easy for man the way, i.e. the way of good or evil, like His saying وهديناه النجدين. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: it may also be accusative as the second object of يسّره, with the hāʾ referring to man, i.e. He made him ready for the way, i.e. He guided him to it. I say: then it must be made to include (taḍmīn) the meaning of أعطى so that it governs two accusatives, or the preposition is omitted, i.e. He made him ready for the way, i.e. guided him to it." What follows is conjoined to it. He said (فأقبره) and did not say فقبره, because القابر is the one who buries with his hand, while المقبر is Allah the Exalted. One says: قبر الميت when he buries him with his own hand, and أقبره when he orders another to put him in a grave. The object of the willing is omitted, the implied form being "when He wills his raising".
(كَلَّا لَمَّا يَقْضِ ما أَمَرَهُ) (كلا) is a rebuke and a restraint for man, who persists in his blindness, deluded by his delusion, overreaching in arrogance through his self-admiration. (لما) is a jussive particle of negation, and (يقض) is an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by (لما), the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the weak letter. It is made jussive by (لما) to indicate that self-admiration and pride have not ceased to cling to man up to the very hour he is in. (ما) is a mafʿūl bihi, and the clause (أمره) is its ṣila (relative clause), with the referring pronoun omitted, i.e. به.
(فَلْيَنْظُرِ الْإِنْسانُ إِلى طَعامِهِ) resumptive speech set out to begin enumerating the successive favours upon man. The lām is the lām of command, (ينظر) is an imperfect verb in the jussive by the lām of command, (الإنسان) is its fāʿil, and (إلى طعامه) is attached to (ينظر).
(أَنَّا صَبَبْنَا الْماءَ صَبًّا) (أنّا) with fatḥa on the hamza; it and what follows are an interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of the genitive as a badal ishtimāl (substitute of inclusion) from (طعامه). The meaning is that pouring the water is a cause of bringing out the food, so it includes it. It was also read with kasra on the hamza, as a resumption explaining how the food is brought about. (أنّ) and its noun; the clause (صببنا) is a verb and its fāʿil, (الماء) is the mafʿūl bihi, and (صبا) is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object).
(ثُمَّ شَقَقْنَا الْأَرْضَ شَقًّا) conjoined to the preceding clause and parsed like it. The secret of attributing the splitting to Him, the Exalted, will come in the section on rhetoric.
(فَأَنْبَتْنا فِيها حَبًّا وَعِنَباً وَقَضْباً وَزَيْتُوناً وَنَخْلًا وَحَدائِقَ غُلْباً وَفاكِهَةً وَأَبًّا) The fāʾ is a conjunction, (أنبتنا) is a verb and its fāʿil, (فيها) is attached to (أنبتنا), (حبا) is a mafʿūl bihi, and what follows is conjoined to it. القضب and القضبة are fresh fodder (al-raṭba).
(مَتاعاً لَكُمْ وَلِأَنْعامِكُمْ) (متاعا) is a maṣdar confirming (أنبتنا), because His causing things to grow is a provision for all living beings; or it is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), the governor being omitted, its implied form being "He did that as a provision for you". (لكم) is attached to (متاعا), and (لأنعامكم) is conjoined to (لكم).
(فَإِذا جاءَتِ الصَّاخَّةُ يَوْمَ يَفِرُّ الْمَرْءُ مِنْ أَخِيهِ وَأُمِّهِ وَأَبِيهِ وَصاحِبَتِهِ وَبَنِيهِ لِكُلِّ امْرِئٍ مِنْهُمْ يَوْمَئِذٍ شَأْنٌ يُغْنِيهِ) The fāʾ is resumptive, and the speech is resumptive, set out to begin explaining their states on the Day of Return. You may also make the fāʾ a conjunction, with the speech conjoined, so as to order what follows it after what preceded it of abundant favours and successive blessings. (إذا) is a future adverb containing the meaning of condition, attached to the omitted apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) understood from His saying (لكل امرئ), the implied form being "each one will be preoccupied with himself". The clause (جاءت) is in the position of the genitive by the adverb's annexation to it, and (الصاخة) is its fāʿil. (يوم) is a badal from (إذا), i.e. the day he flees in it; the clause (يفرّ) is in the position of the genitive by the adverb's annexation to it, (المرء) is its fāʿil, (من أخيه) is attached to (يفر), and what follows is conjoined to (أخيه). (لكل امرئ) is a fronted khabar (predicate), (منهم) is a naʿt (adjective) of (امرئ), and (يومئذ) is an adverb annexed to its like, attached to (يغنيه) [Translator's note: the source prints يفنيه, a misprint for يغنيه]; the tanwīn is a substitute, i.e. on the day when these many things take place. (شأن) is a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject), and the clause (يغنيه) is a naʿt of (شأن).
(وُجُوهٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ مُسْفِرَةٌ ضاحِكَةٌ مُسْتَبْشِرَةٌ) (وجوه) is a mubtadaʾ; what licenses beginning with it although it is indefinite is the division into kinds (al-tanwīʿ). (يومئذ) is an adverb annexed to its like, attached to (مسفرة), and the tanwīn is a substitute for a clause. (مسفرة) is the khabar of (وجوه), and (ضاحكة) and (مستبشرة) are two further khabars of (وجوه).
(وَوُجُوهٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ عَلَيْها غَبَرَةٌ تَرْهَقُها قَتَرَةٌ) The wāw is a conjunction, (وجوه) is a mubtadaʾ, and (يومئذ) is an adverb annexed to its like, attached to (ترهقها). (عليها) is a fronted khabar and (غبرة) a postponed mubtadaʾ, and the clause is the khabar of (وجوه). The clause (ترهقها قترة) is a second khabar of (وجوه): (ترهقها) is an imperfect verb with a fronted mafʿūl bihi, and (قترة) is a postponed mubtadaʾ. [Translator's note: so in the source; (قترة) is in fact the fāʿil of (ترهقها).]
(أُولئِكَ هُمُ الْكَفَرَةُ الْفَجَرَةُ) (أولئك) is a mubtadaʾ; (هم) is a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl) or a second mubtadaʾ; (الكفرة) and (الفجرة) are two khabars of (أولئك) or of (هم), and [in the latter case] the clause is the khabar of (أولئك).

* Rhetoric:
Figurative attribution (al-isnād al-majāzī) in His saying (ثُمَّ شَقَقْنَا الْأَرْضَ شَقًّا): it is a figurative attribution, for the Exalted attributed the splitting to Himself by way of attributing the act to the cause. It has been said that the attribution is literal and that the claim of its figurativeness is one of the doctrines of the Muʿtazila. But al-Bayḍāwī himself follows al-Zamakhsharī in the figurativeness of the attribution, saying: "He attributed the splitting to Himself, the Exalted, as the attribution of the act to the cause." The truth lies with al-Zamakhsharī in this, for its figurativeness does not mean that the acts of servants are created by them, because an act is attributed literally only to the one in whom it subsists, not to the one who brought it into existence; so objecting to it is arbitrary.

dervis-irab:1-17.t:
* Vocabulary:
(تَصَدَّى) its origin is تتصدى, i.e. you expose yourself by turning toward him; المصاداة is opposing. One says تصدى, i.e. he exposed himself; its origin is تصدد from الصدد, which is what faces you and comes to be opposite you, so one of the identical letters was replaced by a weak letter. It is also said to be from الصدى, the sound heard in empty places and hard bodies; and it is said to be from الصدى, which is thirst; the meaning is exposing oneself.

* I'rab:
(عَبَسَ وَتَوَلَّى، أَنْ جاءَهُ الْأَعْمى) عبس and تولى are two past verbs, indeclinable on fatḥa, and their agent is latent, the implied form being "he". It was only brought in these two places, and in a third after them, [in the third person] out of reverence for him, peace be upon him, and gentleness toward him, since in face-to-face address with the tāʾ of the addressee there is something not hidden. [Translator's note: the source sentence is elliptical; the words «in the third person» are supplied to complete the sense, as the source does not state what was brought.] أن جاءه is in the position of accusative as a mafʿūl li-ajlihi, and its governor is either عبس or تولى; جاءه is a past verb and a direct object, and الأعمى the agent. It is better to say that أن and what follows are in the interpretation of a maṣdar, accusative by removal of the preposition, with the preposition and its genitive noun attached to عبس, because coming is not among the verbs of the heart, so one of the conditions for the accusative of the mafʿūl li-ajlihi is defective. (وَما يُدْرِيكَ لَعَلَّهُ يَزَّكَّى أَوْ يَذَّكَّرُ فَتَنْفَعَهُ الذِّكْرى) The wāw is a conjunction; ما is an interrogative noun, in the position of nominative as a mubtadaʾ, and the clause يدريك is the khabar; the kāf is in the position of the first object of يدري and the clause of hope is in the position of the second object. لعله: لعل with its noun, and the clause يزكى, i.e. purifies himself, is the khabar of لعل; it is also said that the second object of يدريك is omitted, implied, the implied form being "what informs you of his affair and the outcome of his state", and the clause لعله يزكى is inceptive. أو is a conjunction; يذكر is conjoined to يزكى; the fāʾ is the fāʾ of causation; تنفعه is an imperfect verb, accusative by an implied أن after the fāʾ of causation, the hāʾ a direct object, and الذكرى the agent. It was also read فتنفعه with nominative, the fāʾ being a conjunction and تنفعه in the nominative conjoined to أو يذكر. (أَمَّا مَنِ اسْتَغْنى فَأَنْتَ لَهُ تَصَدَّى وَما عَلَيْكَ أَلَّا يَزَّكَّى) أما is a particle of condition and detail; من is a relative noun, mubtadaʾ; the clause استغنى is a ṣila with no position; the fāʾ is the connecting one; أنت is an overt detached pronoun in the position of nominative as a mubtadaʾ; له: attached to تصدى; the clause تصدى is the khabar of أنت, and the nominal clause is the khabar of من. The wāw is circumstantial; ما is negative; عليك is a fronted khabar; and أن and what is in its scope is a postponed mubtadaʾ, i.e. "there is no blame upon you in his not purifying himself through Islam". Abū Ḥayyān preferred that ما be interrogative of denial, in which case it is a mubtadaʾ and عليك its khabar, and ألا يزكى is accusative by removal of the preposition, with the preposition and its genitive noun attached to what عليك is attached to, i.e. "settling"; and the clause is a ḥāl from the pronoun in تصدى. (وَأَمَّا مَنْ جاءَكَ يَسْعى، وَهُوَ يَخْشى فَأَنْتَ عَنْهُ تَلَهَّى) The wāw is a conjunction; أما is a particle of condition and detail; من is a relative noun in the position of nominative as a mubtadaʾ; the clause جاءك has no position because it is a ṣila of من; the clause يسعى is a ḥāl from the agent of جاءك; the wāw is circumstantial; هو is a mubtadaʾ and the clause يخشى its khabar; the clause is a ḥāl from the agent of يسعى, hence a nested ḥāl (ḥāl mutadākhila). The fāʾ is the connector of the apodosis of أما; أنت is a mubtadaʾ; عنه: attached to تلهى; تلهى, i.e. تتلهى, is an imperfect verb, nominative, its agent latent, the implied form being "you", and the clause is a khabar; and the clause أنت عنه تلهى is the khabar of من, i.e. "you busy yourself", i.e. it is from لهي بكذا يلهى, meaning to busy oneself with it, and it has nothing to do with اللهو (play), because it is attributed to the pronoun of the Prophet, and it is not fitting to his noble station that the act of play be attributed to him, unlike busying oneself, which may occur from him at times. In al-Qāmūs: «لها لهوا: he played, like التهى; and that ألهاه; and لهي به, like riḍiya: he loved it; and لهي عنه: he forgot, was heedless and left mention of him; and لها, like daʿā, لهيا and لهيانا, and تلهى». (كَلَّا إِنَّها تَذْكِرَةٌ فَمَنْ شاءَ ذَكَرَهُ) كلا is a particle of rebuke and deterrence for every person from committing the like of what was blamed. It is reported that, peace be upon him, he never again frowned in the face of a poor man or exposed himself to a rich one. إن with its noun, and تذكرة is the khabar of إن; the pronoun refers to the admonition or the sūra. The fāʾ is parenthetical; من is a conditional noun that jussives, a mubtadaʾ; شاء is a past verb in the position of jussive, the protasis, and its agent is "he", and the object is omitted, i.e. being admonished; ذكره is a past verb, a latent agent and a direct object, and it is in the position of jussive as the apodosis; and the clause is parenthetical, with no position. (فِي صُحُفٍ مُكَرَّمَةٍ مَرْفُوعَةٍ مُطَهَّرَةٍ بِأَيْدِي سَفَرَةٍ كِرامٍ بَرَرَةٍ) في صحف is a second khabar of إنها; مكرمة and what follows are adjectives of صحف; بأيدي is also an adjective, or a khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ; سفرة is a muḍāf ilayhi and what follows are adjectives. السفرة is the plural of سافر, the scribe, like كاتب and كتبة; "سفرت between the people, أسفر, سفارة": I reconciled them. In al-Mukhtār: «سفر the book: he wrote it, of the pattern ḍaraba». (قُتِلَ الْإِنْسانُ ما أَكْفَرَهُ) The clause is an invocation (duʿāʾ'iyya), with no position; the meaning of قتل is cursed and tormented; الإنسان is a deputy agent; ما is an indefinite complete noun meaning "something", in the position of nominative as a mubtadaʾ; أكفر is a past verb whose agent is obligatorily latent, the implied form being "he" ("here in particular"), and the hāʾ is a direct object. They said "May Allah fight him, how vile he is" and "Allah disgrace him, how unjust he is". The meaning is "wonder at man's disbelief, despite everything we have mentioned after this". It is also said that ما is interrogative, a mubtadaʾ, and the clause أكفره its khabar, i.e. "what thing called him to disbelief?", a question of reproach, but there is no need for this, because it is wonder at his excess in his disbelief, wonder being in relation to creatures, since it is impossible in the case of Allah the Exalted, i.e. he is one of whom "how disbelieving he is!" is said. al-Zamakhsharī has a fine statement: «"ما أكفره" is wonder at his excess in ingratitude for blessings. You will see no style harsher than it, rougher to the touch, more indicative of wrath, further-reaching in blame despite the closeness of its two ends, or more gathering for the imams on the brevity of its body.»

* Benefits:
History relates that ʿAbd Allāh ibn Umm Maktūm ibn Sharīḥ ibn Mālik ibn Rabīʿa al-Fihrī, of Banū ʿĀmir ibn Luʾayy (Umm Maktūm being his father's mother, whose name was ʿĀtika bint ʿĀmir al-Makhzūmī, and he was the son of the maternal aunt of Khadīja bint Khuwaylid). In al-Nawawī's commentary on Muslim, it is that Ibn Umm Maktūm's name was ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr, and Umm Maktūm was the wife of ʿAmr, so she is the mother of ʿAbd Allāh; it is also said that his name was ʿAmr and his father's name is an addition. He came to him while with him were the chiefs of Quraysh, ʿUtba and Shayba, sons of Rabīʿa, Abū Jahl ibn Hishām, al-ʿAbbās ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib, Umayya ibn Khalaf and al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra, and he was calling them to Islam, hoping that those nobles whom he was addressing would accept Islam, so that Islam would be strengthened through them and their followers would become Muslim with their becoming Muslim, and the word of Allah the Exalted would be raised. So he said: "O Messenger of Allah, recite to me and teach me from what Allah the Exalted taught you", and he repeated that, not knowing of his being occupied with the people. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ disliked his interrupting his speech, and frowned and turned away from him; so (the verses) were revealed. After that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to honour him and say when he saw him: "Welcome to him on whose account my Lord rebuked me", and say to him: "Do you have any need?"; and he appointed him as his deputy over Medina twice. al-Qurṭubī said: «All of this is a mistake of the commentators, because Umayya and al-Walīd were in Mecca and Ibn Umm Maktūm was in Medina, he did not attend with the two of them, and they died disbelievers, one before the Hijra and the other at Badr; Umayya never made for Medina nor was he present with him alone or with anyone.» Abū Ḥayyān said: «The mistake is al-Qurṭubī's; how can he deny Ibn Umm Maktūm's attending with them? It is a delusion on his part; they were all of Quraysh, and Ibn Umm Maktūm was there, and the sūra is entirely Meccan by consensus. How can he say "and Ibn Umm Maktūm was in Medina"? He was first in Mecca, then emigrated to Medina, and they were all in Mecca at the time this verse was revealed.» There is another report some have followed, which is that the one spoken of as frowning is not the Prophet ﷺ but a man of Banū Umayya, who frowned when Ibn Umm Maktūm came, because frowning, as al-Sharīf al-Murtaḍā says, is not among his, ﷺ, attributes even toward hostile enemies, let alone believers seeking guidance. The reader will find all this in the longer works; let him return to them if he wishes.

farraa:1-2.t: [126/a] His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿عَبَسَ وَتَوَلَّىٰ أَن جَآءَهُ ٱلأَعْمَىٰ﴾. That was ʿAbd Allāh ibn Umm Maktūm — Umm Maktūm was his father's mother. He came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while there was with him a group of the nobles of Quraysh, to ask about something from which he would benefit; and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ disliked that he should interrupt his talk. So Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He, sent down: ﴿عَبَسَ وَتَوَلَّىٰ﴾, meaning Muhammad ﷺ, ﴿أَن جَآءَهُ ٱلأَعْمَىٰ﴾: because the blind man came to him.

farraa:3-4.t:
Then He, Majestic and Mighty is He, said: ﴿وَمَا يُدْرِيكَ لَعَلَّهُ يَزَّكَّىٰ﴾.
By what he wanted to learn of your knowledge. Then the Prophet ﷺ turned with kindness to Ibn Umm Maktūm [«على أن ابن أم مكتوم» in the source — Translator's note: «أن» appears to be an intrusion], and honoured him after this verse, to the point that he appointed him as his deputy to lead the prayer. The readers agreed on: ﴿فَتَنفَعَهُ ٱلذِّكْرَىٰ﴾ with the nominative [Translator's note: so in the source, although the vowelled quotation shows the accusative فتنفعَه; the readings are reported the other way round elsewhere]; if it were accusative as the response of the fāʾ to لعلّ, it would be correct.
Someone recited to me:
علَّ صروفَ الدَّهر أو دولاتِها * يُدلْنَنَا اللَّمَّة من لَمّاتها
فتستريحَ النفس من زفْراتها * وتُنْقعَ الغلَّةُ من غُلاتها
(Perhaps the vicissitudes of time or its turns will grant us a turn from among its turns, so that the soul may rest from its sighs and the burning thirst be quenched.)
Some read: "أأن جاءه الأعمى" with two hamzas with fatḥa, i.e.: because the blind man came to him he frowned; and it is like His saying: "أأنْ كان ذا مالٍ وبَنِينَ".

farraa:6-6.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَأَنتَ لَهُ تَصَدَّىٰ﴾.
If a reader read: "تَصَدّى" [Translator's note: so in the source; presumably the passive تُصَدَّى is meant], it would be correct.

farraa:11-13.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿كَلاَّ إِنَّهَا تَذْكِرَةٌ﴾.
This sura is a reminder. If you wish, you make the hāʾ a support (ʿimād) because of the feminine of التذكرة.
﴿فَمَن شَآءَ ذَكَرَهُ﴾:
he remembers the Qurʾān; the masculine [pronoun] goes back to the revelation.
﴿فَي صُحُفٍ مُّكَرَّمَةٍ﴾:
because they came down from the Preserved Tablet, raised high with your Lord there, purified; none touches them but the purified. This is like His saying: ﴿فَالْمُدَبِّرَاتِ أَمْراً﴾.
He made [126/b] the angels and the scrolls purified, because purification applies to the scrolls, so He made purification belong to those who carry them as well.

farraa:15-15.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿بِأَيْدِي سَفَرَةٍ﴾.
They are the angels; the singular is سافر. The Arabs say: سفرت بين القوم (I mediated between the people) when you make peace between them. So the angels, when they descend with the revelation of Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He, and His instruction, were made like the envoy (السفير) who makes peace between people. The poet said:
وما أدعُ السِّفارةَ بينَ قومى * وما أمْشى بغشٍّ إن مَشَيْتُ
(I do not abandon mediation among my people, and I do not go about with deceit when I go.)
And البررة: its singular, by analogy in Arabic, is بارّ; because the Arabs do not say فَعَلة intending a plural unless its singular is فاعل, like كافر and كفرة, and فاجر and فجرة. This is the rule, by which its singular is بارّ. What the Arabs [actually] say is: رجل بَرّ (a pious man) and امرأة برّة (a pious woman); then it was given a plural on the interpretation of فاعل, as they said: قوم خَيَرَة بَرَرَة (good, pious people) — I heard it from one of the Arabs — and the singular of الخيرة is خيّر, and of البررة: برّ. Similar to it is: قوم سَراة (noble people), whose singular is سَرِيّ; it ought to have been سارٍ. When the Arabs pluralise سارٍ they pluralise it with a ḍamma on the first letter and say: سُراة and غُزاة. So it is as though, when they said سَراة, they disliked giving its first letter a ḍamma, which would make the singular seem to be سارٍ; so they wanted to distinguish, by the fatḥa on the first letter of سَراة, between السريّ and الساري.

farraa:17-19.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿مَآ أَكْفَرَهُ﴾.
It may be an exclamation of wonder, and it may be: what is it that made him disbelieve? The exegesis came with this second interpretation. Then He made him wonder and said: ﴿مِنْ أَيِّ شَيءٍ خَلَقَهُ﴾. Then [127/a] He explained and said: ﴿مِن نُّطْفَةٍ خَلَقَهُ فَقَدَّرَهُ﴾ — in stages: a drop, then a clot, to the end of his creation; and wretched or happy, and male or female.

farraa:20-20.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ثُمَّ ٱلسَّبِيلَ يَسَّرَهُ﴾.
Its meaning: then He made him at ease with the way (يسّره للسبيل). Similar to it is: ﴿إِنَّا هَدَيْنَاهُ السَّبِيلَ﴾, i.e. We made known to him the way of good and the way of evil.

farraa:21-21.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ثُمَّ أَمَاتَهُ فَأَقْبَرَهُ﴾.
He made him one who is buried, and did not make him one of those thrown to the beasts of prey and the birds, nor one of those placed in ossuaries (النواويس); as though the grave is one of the things by which the Muslim was honoured. He did not say فقبره, because القابر is the one who buries with his hand, while المُقبِر is Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He, because He made him one who has a grave; and His act is not like the act of the human (الآمى) [Translator's note: so in the source; read الآدمي]. The Arabs say: بترتُ ذنب البعير (I cut off the camel's tail), and والله أبتره (and Allah made it tailless).
And عضبت قرن الثور (I broke the bull's horn), and والله أعضبه (Allah made it broken-horned); and طردت فلاناً عني (I drove So-and-so away from me), and والله أطرده, i.e. He made him an outcast. If someone said فقبره, or said of a human أقبره when he directs it in his sense, it would be acceptable and correct. Do you not see that you say: "So-and-so killed his brother", and another says: "Allah killed him"? The Arabs say: هذه كلمة مُقتِلة مُخيفة (this is a word that gets one killed, that brings fear) when whoever says it would be killed; it is said thus, and if one said of it قاتلة خائفة, it would be correct, as you say: هذا الداء قاتلك (this disease is killing you).

farraa:23-23.t:
His saying, Blessed and Exalted is He: ﴿كَلاَّ لَمَّا يَقْضِ مَآ أَمَرَهُ﴾.
He has not fulfilled some of what He commanded him.

farraa:25-25.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَنَّا صَبَبْنَا ٱلْمَآءَ صَبّاً﴾.
Al-Aʿmash and ʿĀṣim read (أنّا), making it in the position of the genitive, i.e.: let him look at Our pouring the water, [i.e.] to [the fact] that We poured, and did such and such. The people of the Ḥijāz and al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī read (إنّا), giving information about the description of the food by way of resumption (istiʾnāf); and both are good. Likewise His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿فَانْظُرْ كَيْفَ كَانَ عَاقبةُ مَكْرِهِمْ أَنَّا دَمَّرْنَاهُمْ﴾ and ﴿إِنا دمرناهم﴾. The position of "أنّا" here in (ʿAbasa), when it has a fatḥa, may also be nominative, as though He resumed and said: his food is Our pouring the water and Our causing such and such to grow.

farraa:27-27.t:
His saying, Blessed and Exalted is He: ﴿حَبّاً﴾.
الحب: all grains — wheat, barley and what is besides them. القضب: fresh fodder (الرطبة); the people of Mecca call fodder (القتّ) القضب. الحدائق: every garden that has a wall around it is a حديقة; what has no wall around it is not called حديقة. الغُلْب: what is thick among the palm trees. الأبّ: what the livestock eat. That is what Ibn ʿAbbās said.

farraa:32-32.t:
His saying, Blessed and Exalted is He: ﴿مَّتَاعاً لَّكُمْ﴾.
That is: We created it as an enjoyment for you and a benefit. If it were nominative, it would be permissible, as we have explained.

farraa:33-33.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ٱلصَّآخَّةُ﴾: the Resurrection.

farraa:34-34.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يَوْمَ يَفِرُّ ٱلْمَرْءُ مِنْ أَخِيهِ﴾.
He flees from his brother: من and عن are the same in it.

farraa:37-37.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لِكُلِّ ٱمْرِىءٍ مِّنْهُمْ يَوْمَئِذٍ شَأْنٌ يُغْنِيهِ﴾.
That is: it occupies him away from his kin. One of the readers read: "يعنيه" (concerns him), and that is anomalous (shādhdh).

farraa:38-38.t:
His saying, Blessed and Exalted is He: ﴿وُجُوهٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ مُّسْفِرَةٌ﴾.
Shining, bright. When a woman casts off her veil or her face-cover, it is said: سفرت, so she is سافر; and one does not say أسفرت.

farraa:41-41.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿تَرْهَقُهَا قَتَرَةٌ﴾.
In speech, قَتْرة, with the tāʾ vowelless, is permissible; but no one has read it so.

harrat-mujtaba:2-2.t: (أن جاءه الأعمى) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] «أنْ» is maṣdariyya (forming a verbal noun); the interpreted maṣdar is accusative by removal of the preposition, the lām.

harrat-mujtaba:3-3.t: The clause «وما يدريك» is conjoined to the clause {عَبَسَ}, and the clause «لعله يزكى» is the second object of «يدريك».

harrat-mujtaba:4-4.t: The fāʾ in «فتنفعه» is causative (sababiyya), and the verb is accusative (manṣūb) by an implied أن as an answer to the hoping (tarajjī); the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) is conjoined to a maṣdar extracted from the preceding speech, i.e.: perhaps there will be a purification with you, and so a benefit.

harrat-mujtaba:5-5.t: «أما»: a particle of condition and detailing; «من»: a relative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject).

harrat-mujtaba:6-6.t: The fāʾ is the linking one; the clause «فأنت له تصدَّى» is the khabar (predicate) of the preceding «من».

harrat-mujtaba:7-7.t: The clause «وما عليك ألا يزكى» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of {تَصَدَّى}; «أن» makes the verb accusative, and the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) «ألا يزكى»: a mubtadaʾ (subject) placed later; the preposition «عليك» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar (predicate), i.e.: his not purifying himself is not upon you.

harrat-mujtaba:8-8.t: The clause «يسعى» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of «جاءك».

harrat-mujtaba:9-9.t: The clause «وهو يخشى» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of {يَسْعَى}.

harrat-mujtaba:10-10.t: The clause «فأنت عنه تلهَّى» is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) «مَنْ».

harrat-mujtaba:12-12.t: The clause «فمن شاء» is parenthetical between the adjective and the noun it qualifies.

harrat-mujtaba:13-13.t: The preposition «في صحف» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) an adjective (ṣifa) of «لتذكرة».

harrat-mujtaba:17-17.t: The clause «قُتِل الإنسان» is resumptive; «ما»: an indefinite noun of wonder (taʿajjub), mubtadaʾ (subject); then a past verb and its object, and the clause is the khabar (predicate) of «ما»; and the clause of wonder is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:18-18.t: The preposition «من أي» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «خلقه», and the clause is resumptive

harrat-mujtaba:19-19.t: The second clause «خلقه» is a badal (substitute) of the first

harrat-mujtaba:20-20.t: «السبيل»: mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an omitted verb explained by what follows it; the implied clause «يسَّره» is conjoined to the clause «قدَّره», and the explicitly stated clause «يسَّره» is explicative

harrat-mujtaba:22-22.t: (ثم إذا شاء أنشره) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The conditional clause is conjoined to the clause «أقبره»

harrat-mujtaba:25-25.t: The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) «أنَّا صببنا» is a badal (substitute) of {طَعَامِهِ}, in the position of the genitive.

harrat-mujtaba:32-32.t: «متاعًا» is mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose); the preposition «لكم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «متاعًا».

harrat-mujtaba:33-33.t: (فإذا جاءت الصاخة) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The conditional clause is resumptive, and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by His saying {لِكُلِّ امْرِئٍ مِنْهُمْ يَوْمَئِذٍ شَأْنٌ يُغْنِيهِ}; the implied form is: "فإذا جاءت اشتغل كل أحد بنفسه" (when it comes, everyone will be busy with himself).

harrat-mujtaba:37-37.t: (لكل امرئ منهم يومئذ شأن يغنيه) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The clause is explicative of the apodosis of «إذا»; the clause «يغنيه» is a naʿt (adjective); the preposition «منهم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt of «امرئ»; «يومئذ» is an adverb attached to the "being" (istiqrār) to which «لكل» is attached.

harrat-mujtaba:38-38.t: «وجوه»: mubtadaʾ (subject); «يومئذ» is an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate) {ضَاحِكَةٌ}; «مسفرة»: naʿt (adjective) of «وجوه».

harrat-mujtaba:40-40.t: «وجوه» is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the clause «عليها غبرة» is a naʿt (adjective) of «وجوه».

harrat-mujtaba:41-41.t: The clause «ترهقها» is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) {وُجُوهٌ}.

harrat-mujtaba:42-42.t: (أولئك هم الكفرة الفجرة) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The clause is resumptive; «هم» is a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl); «الكفرة الفجرة»: two khabars (predicates) of «أولئك».

mekki-muskil:2-2.t: His saying, the Exalted: (أن جاءه الأعمى): (أن) is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose). It is also said that it is in the position of the genitive with an implied lām; and also said that it means (إذ) "when".

mekki-muskil:4-4.t: His saying (فتنفعه الذكرى): whoever reads it in the accusative makes it the answer of (لعل) with the fāʾ, because it is non-affirmative, so it resembles the wish and the question; but this is not recognised by the Basrans. Whoever reads it in the nominative conjoins it to (يذكر).

mekki-muskil:8-8.t: His saying (وأما من جاءك يسعى): (من) is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and (يسعى) is a ḥāl (circumstantial). Likewise (وهو يخشى) is a mubtadaʾ and khabar (predicate), also in the position of a ḥāl.

mekki-muskil:10-10.t: His saying (فأنت عنه تلهى): a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate), in the position of the khabar of (من). Its like is (أما من استغنى فأنت له تصدى).

mekki-muskil:20-20.t:
His saying (ثم السبيل يسره): the hāʾ and (السبيل) are two objects of (يسره), with the lām omitted from (السبيل), i.e. "then for the way He made him at ease".
His saying (ما أكفره): (ما) is an interrogative, a mubtadaʾ (subject), and (أكفره) is the khabar (predicate), in the sense "What thing led him to disbelief, despite the signs he sees indicating the oneness [of Allah]?" (ما) may also be a mubtadaʾ expressing wonder (taʿajjub), i.e. he is one at whom one wonders, so it is said of him "How ungrateful he is!", with (أكفره) the khabar as well.

mekki-muskil:25-25.t: His saying (أنا صببنا): whoever reads (أن) with fatḥa makes it in the position of the genitive with an implied lām, i.e. "because We" (لأنا). It is also said: in the position of the accusative because the lām is absent. It is also said: in the position of the genitive as a badal (substitute) from (الطعام), because these things include the food, which comes into being from them, since the meaning of (إلى طعامه) is "to the coming into being of his food, how it comes about". So the inclusion here is of the second within the first [Translator's note: i.e. a badal ishtimāl], because the consideration is only of the things from which food comes into being, not of the food itself.

mekki-muskil:32-32.t: His saying (متاعا لكم): accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun).

muyesser-irab:1-1.t:
﴿عبس﴾: a past verb indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa; the fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "huwa" (he).
﴿وتولى﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and «تولى» is a past verb indeclinable on a fatḥa implied (muqaddar) on the alif; the fāʿil is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "huwa" (he); the clause ﴿عبس﴾ is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), and the clause ﴿تولى﴾ is conjoined to the clause ﴿عبس﴾.

muyesser-irab:2-2.t:
﴿أن﴾: maṣdar-forming (maṣdariyya).
﴿جاءه﴾: a past verb, and the hāʾ is mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the interpreted maṣdar is accusative (manṣūb) by removal of the preposition.
﴿الأعمى﴾: the fāʿil (agent) of «جاء».

muyesser-irab:3-3.t:
﴿وما﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and «ما» is an interrogative noun in the position of a nominative (marfūʿ), mubtadaʾ (subject).
﴿يدريك﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative; the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "anta" (you) [Translator's note: so in the source; the latent fāʿil of «يدريك» would more naturally be "huwa", referring back to «ما»]; and the kāf is the first mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿لعله﴾: «لعل» is a particle of hope and of the accusative, and the hāʾ is its noun.
﴿يزكى﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative; the fāʿil is latent, its implied form being "huwa" (he); the clause ﴿يزكي﴾ [sic in the source, for «يزكى»] is the khabar (predicate) of ﴿لعل﴾, and the clause ﴿لعله يزكى﴾ is in the position of an accusative, standing in place of the second and third objects of the verb ﴿يدريك﴾.

muyesser-irab:4-4.t:
﴿أو﴾: a conjunction.
﴿يذكر﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ); the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "huwa" (he); the clause ﴿يذكر﴾ is conjoined to the clause ﴿يزكى﴾.
﴿فتنفعه﴾: the fāʾ is causal (sababiyya), and «تنفع» is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by «أن» implied after the causal fāʾ; the hāʾ is mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the interpreted maṣdar from «أن» and the verb is conjoined to a maṣdar understood from the preceding speech, i.e. "perhaps there will be with you a purification, and then a benefit".
﴿الذكرى﴾: the fāʿil of «تنفع», nominative by an implied (muqaddar) ḍamma.

muyesser-irab:5-5.t:
﴿أما﴾: «أما» is a particle of condition and detailing.
﴿من﴾: a relative noun in the position of a nominative (marfūʿ), mubtadaʾ (subject).
﴿استغنى﴾: a past verb; the fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "huwa" (he); the clause ﴿استغنى﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:6-6.t:
﴿فأنت﴾: an overt, detached pronoun in the position of a nominative (marfūʿ), mubtadaʾ (subject).
﴿له﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿تصدى﴾.
﴿تصدى﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative; the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "anta" (you); the clause ﴿تصدى﴾ is the khabar (predicate) of ﴿أنت﴾.

muyesser-irab:7-7.t:
﴿وما﴾: the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and «ما» is negating.
﴿عليك﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted fronted khabar (predicate).
﴿ألا﴾: «أن» is maṣdar-forming (maṣdariyya), and «لا» is negating.
﴿يزكى﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) [Translator's note: so in the source; after «أن» the verb is accusative, the fatḥa being implied on the alif]; the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "huwa" (he); the interpreted maṣdar is a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject).

muyesser-irab:8-8.t:
﴿وأما﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and «أما» is a particle of condition and detailing.
﴿من﴾: a relative noun in the position of a nominative (marfūʿ), mubtadaʾ (subject).
﴿جاءك﴾: a past verb; the fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, and the kāf is mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause ﴿جاءك﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position.
﴿يسعى﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative; the fāʿil is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "huwa" (he); the clause ﴿يسعى﴾ is in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil of ﴿جاءك﴾.

muyesser-irab:9-9.t:
﴿وهو﴾: the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and «هو» is mubtadaʾ (subject).
﴿يخشى﴾: an imperfect verb; the fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "huwa" (he); the clause is in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).

muyesser-irab:10-10.t:
﴿فأنت﴾: the fāʾ is a particle in the apodosis of ﴿أما﴾, and «أنت» is a detached pronoun in the position of a nominative (marfūʿ), mubtadaʾ (subject).
﴿عنه﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿تلهى﴾.
﴿تلهى﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative; its fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "anta" (you); the clause ﴿تلهى﴾ is the khabar (predicate) of «أنت», and the clause ﴿أنت عنه تلهى﴾ is the khabar of ﴿من﴾.

muyesser-irab:11-11.t:
﴿كلا﴾: a particle of deterrence and rebuke.
﴿إنها﴾: «إن» is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa, and ﴿ها﴾ is its noun.
﴿تذكرة﴾: the khabar (predicate) of «إن», nominative (marfūʿ); the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:12-12.t:
﴿فمن﴾: the fāʾ is parenthetical, and «من» is a jussive-governing conditional noun, mubtadaʾ (subject).
﴿شاء﴾: a past verb in the position of a jussive (majzūm), the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); its fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "huwa" (he).
﴿ذكره﴾: a past verb; the fāʿil is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "huwa" (he), and the hāʾ is mafʿūl bihi (direct object); it is in the position of a jussive, the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); the clause is parenthetical between the thing described, namely His saying ﴿تذكرة﴾, and the description, namely His saying ﴿في صحف﴾, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:13-13.t:
﴿في﴾: a preposition.
﴿صحف﴾: a noun in the genitive, the sign of its genitive being the kasra; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted adjective (ṣifa) of ﴿تذكرة﴾.
﴿مكرمة﴾: a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿صحف﴾, genitive (majrūr).

muyesser-irab:14-14.t:
﴿مرفوعة﴾: a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿صحف﴾, genitive (majrūr).
﴿مطهرة﴾: a naʿt of ﴿صحف﴾, genitive.

muyesser-irab:15-15.t:
﴿بأيدي﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted naʿt (adjective) of ﴿صحف﴾.
﴿سفرة﴾: muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr).

muyesser-irab:16-16.t:
﴿كرام﴾: a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿سفرة﴾, genitive (majrūr).
﴿بررة﴾: a naʿt of ﴿سفرة﴾, genitive.

muyesser-irab:17-17.t:
﴿قتل﴾: a past verb, passive (built for that whose agent is not named).
﴿الإنسان﴾: nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), nominative (marfūʿ).
﴿ما﴾: a complete indefinite (nakira tāmma) meaning "a great thing", in the position of a nominative, mubtadaʾ (subject).
﴿أكفره﴾: a past verb indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa; its fāʿil (agent) is a necessarily latent (mustatir wujūban) pronoun, its implied form being "huwa" (it); and the hāʾ is mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause ﴿أكفره﴾ is in the position of a nominative, the khabar (predicate) of «ما»; and the clause ﴿قتل...﴾ is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:18-18.t:
﴿من﴾: a preposition indeclinable (mabnī) on sukūn.
﴿أي﴾: a noun in the genitive; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿خلقه﴾.
﴿شيء﴾: muḍāf ilayhi.
﴿خلقه﴾: «خلق» is a past verb indeclinable on fatḥa; its fāʿil (agent) is a necessarily latent (mustatir wujūban) pronoun, its implied form being "huwa" (He); and the hāʾ is mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:19-19.t:
﴿من﴾: a preposition indeclinable (mabnī) on sukūn.
﴿نطفة﴾: a noun in the genitive; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿خلقه﴾, and ﴿من نطفة﴾ is a badal (substitute) from His saying ﴿من أي شيء﴾.
﴿خلقه﴾: «خلق» is a past verb indeclinable on fatḥa; its fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "huwa" (He); and the hāʾ is mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿فقدره﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and «قدره» is a past verb indeclinable on fatḥa; its fāʿil is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "huwa" (He); and the hāʾ is mafʿūl bihi.

muyesser-irab:20-20.t:
﴿ثم﴾: a conjunction for sequence and delay.
﴿السبيل﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb) by preoccupation (ʿalā al-ishtighāl), by an implied (muqaddar) verb indicated by what follows it.
﴿يسره﴾: «يسر» is a past verb indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa; its fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "huwa" (He); and the hāʾ is mafʿūl bihi. The clause ﴿يسره﴾ is explicative (tafsīriyya), with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:21-21.t:
﴿ثم﴾: a conjunction for sequence and delay.
﴿أماته﴾: «أمات» is a past verb indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa; its fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "huwa" (He); and the hāʾ is mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿فأقبره﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and «أقبره» is a past verb indeclinable on fatḥa; its fāʿil is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "huwa" (He); and the hāʾ is mafʿūl bihi; the clause ﴿أقبره﴾ is conjoined to ﴿أماته﴾.

muyesser-irab:22-22.t:
﴿ثم﴾: a conjunction.
﴿إذا﴾: an adverb (ẓarf) for future time, containing the meaning of condition, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أنشره﴾.
﴿شاء﴾: a past verb; the fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "huwa" (He); the clause ﴿شاء﴾ is in the position of a genitive, the adverb being put in construct with it.
﴿أنشره﴾: a past verb; the fāʿil is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "huwa" (He), and the hāʾ is mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause ﴿أنشره﴾ is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of the non-jussive condition.

muyesser-irab:23-23.t:
﴿كلا﴾: a particle of deterrence and rebuke.
﴿لما﴾: a jussive-governing particle of negation.
﴿يقض﴾: an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm); the fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "huwa" (he); the clause ﴿لما يقض...﴾ is resumptive, with no grammatical position.
﴿ما﴾: a relative, mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿أمره﴾: a past verb; the fāʿil is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "huwa" (He), and the hāʾ is mafʿūl bihi; the clause ﴿أمره﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿ما﴾, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:24-24.t:
﴿فلينظر﴾: the fāʾ is resumptive, the lām is the lām of command, and «ينظر» is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the lām of command.
﴿الإنسان﴾: fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the ḍamma; the clause ﴿فلينظر الإنسان﴾ is resumptive, with no grammatical position.
﴿إلى﴾: a preposition.
﴿طعامه﴾: a noun in the genitive, and the hāʾ is in the position of a genitive, muḍāf ilayhi; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿ينظر﴾.

muyesser-irab:25-25.t:
﴿أنا﴾: «أن» is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), and ﴿نا﴾ is its noun.
﴿صببنا﴾: a past verb, and ﴿نا﴾ is a pronoun in the position of a nominative, fāʿil (agent); the clause ﴿صببنا﴾ is in the position of a nominative, khabar (predicate); and ﴿أنا صببنا﴾ is in the position of a genitive, a badal (substitute) from «طعامه».
﴿الماء﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb), the sign of its accusative being the fatḥa.
﴿صبا﴾: mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), accusative, the sign of its accusative being the fatḥa.

muyesser-irab:26-26.t:
﴿ثم﴾: a conjunction for sequence with delay.
﴿شققنا﴾: a past verb, and ﴿نا﴾ is the fāʿil (agent).
﴿الأرض﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb).
﴿شقا﴾: mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), accusative; the clause ﴿ثم شققنا﴾ is conjoined to the previous clause, in the position of a nominative.

muyesser-irab:27-27.t:
﴿فأنبتنا﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and «أنبتنا» is a past verb and its fāʿil (agent).
﴿فيها﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أنبتنا﴾.
﴿حبا﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object).

muyesser-irab:28-28.t:
﴿وعنبا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and «عنبا» is a noun conjoined to ﴿حبا﴾, accusative (manṣūb).
﴿وقضبا﴾: conjoined to ﴿حبا﴾, accusative.

muyesser-irab:29-29.t:
﴿وزيتونا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and «زيتونا» is a noun conjoined to ﴿حبا﴾, accusative (manṣūb).
﴿ونخلا﴾: conjoined to ﴿حبا﴾, accusative.

muyesser-irab:30-30.t:
﴿وحدائق﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and «حدائق» is a noun conjoined to ﴿حبا﴾, accusative (manṣūb).
﴿غلبا﴾: a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿حدائق﴾, accusative.

muyesser-irab:31-31.t:
﴿وفاكهة﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and «فاكهة» is a noun conjoined to ﴿حبا﴾, accusative (manṣūb).
﴿وأبا﴾: conjoined to ﴿حبا﴾, accusative.

muyesser-irab:32-32.t:
﴿متاعا﴾: mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), accusative (manṣūb); or standing in for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb, because it is a noun of the maṣdar (ism maṣdar), the implied form being: "He gives you provision".
﴿لكم﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿متاعا﴾.
﴿ولأنعامكم﴾: the wāw is a conjunction and the lām is a preposition; «أنعامكم» is a noun in the genitive, and the pronoun is in the position of a genitive, muḍāf ilayhi; ﴿لأنعامكم﴾ is conjoined to ﴿لكم﴾.

muyesser-irab:33-33.t:
﴿فإذا﴾: the fāʾ is resumptive or a conjunction, the speech being resumptive with no grammatical position, or conjoined; «إذا» is an accusative adverb (ẓarf) of the future, containing the meaning of condition, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted apodosis.
﴿جاءت﴾: a past verb, the tāʾ being for the feminine.
﴿الصاخة﴾: fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ); the clause «جاءت» is in the position of a genitive, the adverb being put in construct with it.

muyesser-irab:34-34.t:
﴿يوم﴾: a badal (substitute) from ﴿إذا﴾, accusative (manṣūb), i.e. "[the day] in which he flees".
﴿يفر﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ).
﴿المرء﴾: fāʿil (agent), nominative; the clause ﴿يفر﴾ is in the position of a genitive, the adverb being put in construct with it.
﴿من﴾: a preposition.
﴿أخيه﴾: a noun in the genitive by the yāʾ, because it is one of the six nouns; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يفر﴾.

muyesser-irab:35-35.t:
﴿وأمه﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and «أمه» is a noun conjoined to ﴿أخيه﴾, genitive (majrūr) by the kasra.
﴿وأبيه﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and «أبيه» is a noun conjoined to ﴿أخيه﴾, genitive by the yāʾ.

muyesser-irab:36-36.t:
﴿وصاحبته﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and «صاحبته» is a noun conjoined to ﴿أخيه﴾, genitive (majrūr) by the kasra.
﴿وبنيه﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and «بنيه» is a noun conjoined to ﴿أخيه﴾, genitive by the yāʾ.

muyesser-irab:37-37.t:
﴿لكل﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted nominative fronted khabar (predicate).
﴿امرئ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr).
﴿منهم﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of ﴿امرئ﴾, genitive.
﴿يومئذ﴾: «يوم» is an adverb of time (ẓarf zamān), attached to the omitted khabar or attached to ﴿يغنيه﴾; and «إذٍ» is a noun indeclinable (mabnī) on a sukūn implied (muqaddar) because its place is occupied by the tanwīn of compensation, in the position of a genitive, muḍāf ilayhi; the tanwīn compensates for an omitted clause.
﴿شأن﴾: a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ).
﴿يغنيه﴾: an imperfect verb and a latent (mustatir) fāʿil (agent), and the hāʾ is mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause ﴿يغنيه﴾ is a naʿt of ﴿شأن﴾, nominative.

muyesser-irab:38-38.t:
﴿وجوه﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ).
﴿يومئذ﴾: «يوم» is an adverb of time (ẓarf zamān), attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿مسفرة﴾; and «إذٍ» is a noun indeclinable (mabnī) on a sukūn implied (muqaddar) because its place is occupied by the tanwīn of compensation, in the position of a genitive, muḍāf ilayhi; the tanwīn compensates for an omitted clause.
﴿مسفرة﴾: khabar (predicate), nominative.

muyesser-irab:39-39.t:
﴿ضاحكة﴾: a second khabar (predicate), nominative (marfūʿ).
﴿مستبشرة﴾: a third khabar of ﴿وجوه﴾.

muyesser-irab:40-40.t:
﴿ووجوه﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and «وجوه» is conjoined to the first ﴿وجوه﴾, nominative (marfūʿ).
﴿يومئذ﴾: «يوم» is an adverb of time (ẓarf zamān), attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted khabar (predicate) to which the preposition and its genitive noun ﴿عليها﴾ are attached; and «إذٍ» is a noun indeclinable (mabnī) on a sukūn implied (muqaddar) because its place is occupied by the tanwīn of compensation, in the position of a genitive, muḍāf ilayhi; the tanwīn compensates for an omitted clause.
﴿عليها﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted fronted khabar.
﴿غبرة﴾: a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative; the clause ﴿عليها غبرة﴾ is in the position of a nominative, a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿وجوه﴾ or a second khabar of it.

muyesser-irab:41-41.t:
﴿ترهقها﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and a fronted mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿قترة﴾: a postponed fāʿil (agent), nominative; the clause ﴿ترهقها﴾ is in the position of a nominative, the khabar (predicate) of the second ﴿وجوه﴾.

muyesser-irab:42-42.t:
﴿أولئك﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ).
﴿هم﴾: a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl).
﴿الكفرة﴾: the khabar (predicate) of ﴿أولئك﴾.
﴿الفجرة﴾: a second khabar of ﴿أولئك﴾. Or ﴿هم﴾ is a mubtadaʾ, «الكفرة» a first khabar and «الفجرة» a second khabar, and the clause is the khabar of ﴿أولئك﴾.

nahhas-irab:10-10.t: The original is تتلهّى, i.e. you busy yourself [with something else]. He ﷺ did this seeking the polytheist's acceptance of Islam.

nahhas-irab:12-12.t: [ذَكَرَهُ is masculine] because it is a non-real feminine. [Translator's note: i.e. the pronoun refers to تذكرة, whose feminine gender is grammatical, not real.]

nahhas-irab:13-15.t: It was said: by it [the honoured pages] is meant the Preserved Tablet. This is according to the interpretation of Ibn ʿAbbās, because Saʿīd ibn Jubayr related from him concerning the meaning of بِأَيْدِي سَفَرَةٍ (15) that they are the angels. ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa related from him that they are the scribes. Qatāda said: they are the reciters. The correct view is the first; it is well known in the speech of the Arabs that one says سفر الرجل بين القوم when he went as an envoy between them to make peace. The angels are سفرة because they are the messengers of Allah the Exalted to His prophets, Allah's blessings be upon them, and they are also scribes who record the deeds of the servants. So all this is not contradictory — except that Wahb ibn Munabbih said: السّفرة الكرام البررة are the Companions of Muḥammad ﷺ. بررة is the plural of بارّ, and أبرار is the plural of برّ.

nahhas-irab:17-17.t: Mujāhid said: When Allah the Exalted says "man has been killed (قتل الإنسان)", or [something else] was done to him, it is the disbeliever. The meaning of قتل is "destroyed", because the one killed is destroyed. It was also said: قتل means "cursed". ما أكفره: it is preferable that «ما» be interrogative, i.e. "what has made him disbelieve", despite the manifestness of the signs of Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He, and His favour to him. It was also said: it is an exclamation (taʿajjub).

nahhas-irab:18-20.t: مِنْ نُطْفَةٍ خَلَقَهُ: i.e. he was only created from something filthy, and he only becomes noble through obedience to Allah. The best of what has been said about the meaning of ثُمَّ السَّبِيلَ يَسَّرَهُ (20) is the view of ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Zubayr, may Allah have mercy on him, that He made it easy for him, i.e. made it easy for him until he came out of the womb. The implied form in Arabic is "then for the way", the lām being omitted because it is a verb that takes two objects, one of them by means of a particle.

nahhas-irab:2-2.t: أَنْ is in the position of the accusative, i.e. لأن ("because"). Some grammarians say: its position is genitive, by an implied lām. And some of them say: «أن» means «إذ» ("when").

nahhas-irab:21-21.t:
That is, He made him one who has a grave, i.e. [He ordered] that he be buried. As for the one who buries, he is called قابر, as the poet said: [al-sarīʿ] 539-
لو أسندت ميتا إلى نحرها ... عاش ولم يتنقل إلى قابر»
(If she leaned a dead man against her throat, he would live and not be carried to a burier.) [Translator's note: the source has a stray closing «»» after the verse, and reads يتنقل where the verse is usually cited as ينقل.]

nahhas-irab:22-22.t:
That is, He brings him to life; the implied form is "when He wills, He will raise him". One says أنشره الله فنشر ("Allah revived him and he revived"), so he is منشر and ناشر, as the poet said: [al-sarīʿ] 540-
حتّى يقول النّاس ممّا رأوا ... يا عجبا للميّت النّاشر
(Until people say, from what they have seen: How wondrous is the dead man come back to life!)

nahhas-irab:23-23.t: Some grammarians make «كلّا» a complete stop (tamām) throughout the whole Qur'an, i.e. "No! The matter is not as the disbeliever says, 'I have fulfilled what was due from me.'" Some grammarians make it a beginning [of a new sentence] throughout the whole Qur'an, and some distinguish [case by case]. This will be explained under the complete stops (al-tamām), Allah willing.

nahhas-irab:24-26.t:
[إِلى طَعامِهِ] is a complete stop (tamām) according to the reading of the Medinans and Abū ʿAmr [إِنَّا]; according to the reading of the Kufans it is not a complete stop, because they read أَنَّا, meaning لأنّا ("because We"). It cannot be a badal (substitute) for طعام as Abū ʿUbayd interpreted it, because the grammarians have set out the kinds of badal and this does not come under them.
The meaning of صَبًّا and شَقًّا is tawkīd (emphasis), and likewise these maṣdars (verbal nouns).
