nahhas-irab:27-31.t: It is related from Ibn ʿAbbās that he said in the presence of ʿUmar: The plants of the earth are seven. [ʿUmar] said to him: I do not understand what you are saying. He said: فَأَنْبَتْنا فِيها حَبًّا (27) وَعِنَباً وَقَضْباً (28) وَزَيْتُوناً وَنَخْلًا (29) وَحَدائِقَ غُلْباً (30) — i.e. intertwined — وَفاكِهَةً وَأَبًّا (31) — i.e. pasture for the livestock. ʿUmar said: This is how you should speak, as this young man speaks. Ibn Abī Ṭalḥa related from him: الأبّ is what is soft among the fruits. [Translator's note: «ما لأن» in the source is read as «ما لان».]

nahhas-irab:3-3.t: The original is يتزكّى; the tāʾ was assimilated into the zāy.

nahhas-irab:32-32.t: [مَتاعاً is] accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun).

nahhas-irab:33-33.t: Ibn Abī Ṭalḥa related from Ibn ʿAbbās that he said: [الصَّاخَّةُ is] the Resurrection. ʿIkrima said: the first blast. Al-Ḥasan said: everything listens intently (يصيخ) to it, i.e. everything falls silent for it.

nahhas-irab:34-36.t: It was said: they flee because of the claims they have against one another, and they fear that. It was also said: they flee because they are ashamed before one another and dislike that [the other] should see the disgrace that befalls him.

nahhas-irab:37-37.t: That is, it occupies him so that he cannot attend to others.

nahhas-irab:38-38.t: وُجُوهٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ: [وجوه] is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), even though it is indefinite, because of the information it carries; the khabar (predicate) is مُسْفِرَةٌ.

nahhas-irab:39-39.t: [ضاحِكَةٌ مُسْتَبْشِرَةٌ are] naʿt (adjective). Ibn Zayd said: القترة is the dust that rises up. It is related that when the beasts are told, "Become dust", that dust becomes a dust-cloud (غبرة) on the faces of the disbelievers.

nahhas-irab:4-4.t:
The original is يتذكر; the tāʾ was assimilated into the dhāl because of its closeness to it. فَتَنْفَعَهُ الذِّكْرى: al-Farrāʾ claimed that the accusative is permissible but was not read. Abū Jaʿfar said: The transmission is well known from ʿĀṣim that he read فَتَنْفَعَهُ الذِّكْرى in the accusative. The Kufans say: it is an answer to لعلّ, while the Basrans do not recognise an answer to لعلّ in the accusative. They and the Kufans have both reported what requires the accusative, namely the command, the prohibition, the negation, the wish and the question; the Kufans added the supplication; and they did not mention the answer to لعل among these answers. I asked Abū al-Ḥasan ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān about it, and he said: I know no justification for the accusative, even though ʿĀṣim, with his eminence, read it — except that «أو» may make what follows it accusative, as the poet said: [al-ṭawīl] 538-
فقلت له لا تبك عينك إنّما ... نحاول ملكا أو نموت فنعذرا
(I said to him: let not your eye weep; we are only seeking a kingdom, or we die and are excused.)
So it may be that it is conjoined to what is made accusative after «أو». [Translator's note: the connection to أو is not explained further in the source.]

nahhas-irab:42-42.t: هم may be a separating pronoun (fāṣila) or a mubtadaʾ (subject); الْفَجَرَةُ is the khabar (predicate), and the clause is the khabar of أولئك.

nahhas-irab:5-6.t: فَأَنْتَ لَهُ تَصَّدَّى is the reading of the Medinans; the original is تتصدّى, then it was assimilated. The reading of the Kufans and Abū ʿAmr is تَصَدَّى with the omission of a tāʾ, so as not to combine two tāʾs. [Translator's note: the source prints both readings as «تَصَدَّى»; the Medinan reading, by the explanation given, has the doubled ṣād.]

nahhas-irab:8-8.t: [يَسْعى] is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), and likewise

nahhas-irab:9-9.t: [وَهُوَ يَخْشى]. It is also possible that the clause is another khabar (predicate). [Translator's note: this entry continues the sentence of the previous one.]

safi-cedvel:24-32.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) resumptive [Note: or connecting the apodosis of an omitted conditional] , (اللام) is the lām of command, (إلى طعامه) attached to (ينظر), (صبّا) is an accusative mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object).
The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) (أنّا صببنا..) is in the position of a genitive, a badal ishtimāl (inclusive substitute) for طعامه.
Clause: «لينظر الإنسان ... » has no grammatical position, resumptive [Note: or it is the apodosis of an omitted conditional, i.e.: if you wish to know the power of Allah and His management, then let the human being look ...] .
And the clause: «صببنا ... » is in the position of a nominative, the khabar (predicate) of أنّ.
26-32 (ثمّ) is a conjunction, and likewise (الفاء) and (الواو) in the four places; (شقّا) is an accusative mafʿūl muṭlaq; (فيها) is attached to (أنبتنا); (حدائق) is denied tanwīn because it is of the form of the "furthest limit of plurals" (a diptote); (متاعا) is a mafʿūl muṭlaq of an omitted verb, i.e. "He gave you enjoyment with that, as an enjoyment" [Note: see (33) of Sūrat al-Nāziʿāt.] , (لكم) is attached to (متاعا), and likewise (لأنعامكم) ..
And the clause: «شققنا ... » is in the position of a nominative, conjoined to the clause صببنا.
And the clause: «أنبتنا ... » is in the position of a nominative, conjoined to the clause شققنا.

* Morphology:
(25) صبّا: a samāʿī (heard, non-rule-based) maṣdar of the triliteral صبّ, on the pattern فعل (with fatḥa then sukūn); its ʿayn and lām are the same letter.
(26) شقّا: a samāʿī maṣdar of the triliteral شقّ, on the pattern فعل (with fatḥa then sukūn); its ʿayn and lām are the same letter.
(28) قضبا: a noun for fresh, tender herbage, on the pattern فعل (with fatḥa then sukūn).
(30) غلبا: a noun for thick, densely entwined trees, on the pattern فعل (with ḍamma then sukūn).
(31) أبّا: a noun for dry herbage, and it is said to be chaff (straw), on the pattern فعل (with fatḥa then sukūn).

* Rhetoric:
Figurative attribution (al-isnād al-majāzī): in His saying, the Exalted, «ثُمَّ شَقَقْنَا الْأَرْضَ شَقًّا» .
Attributing it to His pronoun is a figure of speech, of the kind of attribution to the cause, even though Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is in reality the Originator; the attribution of an act is literally to the one by whom it is carried out, not to the one from whom it issues as an act of origination.

safi-cedvel:33-37.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) resumptive, and the apodosis of إذا is omitted; (يوم) is an accusative adverb of time, a badal (substitute) for (إذا); (من أخيه) is attached to (يفرّ); (الواو) is a conjunction in the four places; (لكلّ) is attached to an advanced khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) (شأن); (منهم) is attached to an adjective of لكلّ امرئ; (يومئذ) is an adverb, accusative (or indeclinable), annexed to an indeclinable adverb, attached to the existence (istiqrār) to which لكلّ is attached..
Clause: «جاءت الصاخّة ... » is in the position of a genitive, muḍāf ilayhi (the second term of a genitive construct). The apodosis is omitted, i.e. "each will be preoccupied with himself".
And the clause: «يفرّ المرء ... » is in the position of a genitive, muḍāf ilayhi.
And the clause: «لكلّ امرئ منهم شأنه ... » has no grammatical position, an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
And the clause: «يغنيه ... » is in the position of a nominative, a naʿt (adjective) of شأن.

* Morphology:
(33) الصاخّة: a noun meaning the calamity that deafens (taṣukku) creatures, i.e. they listen to it, and it is the second blast; in al-Mukhtār: "al-ṣākhkha is the cry that deafens by its intensity". It is on the pattern of the active participle, and the tāʾ is for intensification.
(36) صاحبته: the feminine of صاحب, an active participle of the triliteral صحب, on the pattern فاعل.

safi-cedvel:38-42.t:
* I'rab:
(وجوه) is a nominative mubtadaʾ (subject) [Note: the indefinite noun was qualified, so it was permissible to parse it as a mubtadaʾ..] , (يومئذ): its parsing has passed [Note: in the preceding verse (37) .] ; it is attached to the khabar (predicate) (ضاحكة), (مسفرة) is a nominative naʿt (adjective) of وجوه.
Clause: «وجوه ... ضاحكة ... » has no grammatical position, resumptive.
40-42 (الواو) is a conjunction; (وجوه يومئذ..) is like the first; (عليها) is attached to an advanced khabar of the mubtadaʾ (غبرة); (هم) is a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl)..
And the clause: «وجوه ... عليها غبرة» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the resumptive one.
And the clause: «عليها غبرة» is in the position of a nominative, a naʿt of وجوه.
And the clause: «ترهقها قترة ... » is in the position of a nominative, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (وجوه) .
And the clause: «أولئك ... الكفرة» has no grammatical position, resumptive.

* Morphology:
(38) مسفرة: the feminine of مسفر, an active participle of the quadriliteral أسفر meaning "to shine", on the pattern مفعل (with ḍamma on the mīm and kasra on the ʿayn).
(39) مستبشرة: the feminine of مستبشر, an active participle of the sextiliteral استبشر, on the pattern مستفعل (with ḍamma on the mīm and kasra on the ʿayn).
(40) غبرة: a noun for dust or its fine part, on the pattern فعلة (with three fatḥas).
(41) قترة: a noun for darkness and blackness, or for what rises of dust into the sky, on the pattern فعلة (with three fatḥas).
(42) الفجرة: plural of فاجر, an active participle of the triliteral فجر, on the pattern فاعل; the plural is فعلة (with three fatḥas).

safi-cedvel:1-4.t:
* I'rab:
(أن) a maṣdar particle. (الواو) conjunction. (ما) an interrogative noun in the position of nominative, a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is the clause يدريك..
And the interpreted maṣdar (أن جاءه الأعمى) is in the position of genitive by an omitted preposition, namely (اللام), attached to (عبس وتولّى), i.e. "because the blind man came to him".
Clause: «عبس ... » has no grammatical position; it is an initial clause.
And the clause: «تولّى ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the initial clause.
And the clause: «جاءه الأعمى ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the particle-type relative (أن).
And the clause: «ما يدريك ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the initial clause [Note: In the discourse there is an iltifāt from the third person to the second].
And the clause: «يدريك ... » is in the position of nominative, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (ما).
And the clause: «لعلّه يزّكّى ... » is in the position of accusative, a second object of the verb يدريك.
And the clause: «يزّكّى ... » is in the position of nominative, the khabar of «لعنّ» [Translator's note: the source reads «لعنّ», evidently a misprint for لعلّ].
4- (أو) a conjunction. (الفاء) the fāʾ of causation. (تنفعه) an imperfect verb, accusative by an implied أن after the fāʾ.
And the interpreted maṣdar (أن تنفعه..) is in the position of nominative, conjoined to a maṣdar extracted from the preceding expression of hope, i.e. "perhaps with you there is purification or reminding, and so benefit from the reminder"..
And the clause: «يذّكّر ... » is in the position of nominative, conjoined to the clause يزّكّى.
And the clause: «تنفعه الذكرى» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the implied particle-type relative (أن).

* Morphology:
(1) تولّى: it contains an iʿlāl by substitution; its original is تولّي; the yāʾ was vowelled after a fatḥa and was changed into alif.
(3) يزّكّى: it contains the substitution of the tāʾ of tafaʿʿul by zāy for homogeneity; its original is يتزكّى, then it was assimilated into the fāʾ of the word after being made sākin; its wazn is يتفعّل.. and it contains an iʿlāl by substitution, its original being يتزكّي – with a yāʾ at the end – the yāʾ was vowelled after a fatḥa and was changed into alif.
(4) يذّكّر: it contains the substitution of the tāʾ of tafaʿʿul by dhāl for homogeneity, its analogy being that of يزّكّى.

* Benefits:
- Guidance and reproach:
The reason for the revelation of the verses is that ʿAbd Allāh ibn Umm Maktūm – whose name is ʿAmr; and it was said: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sharīḥ ibn Mālik ibn Rabīʿa; and it was said: ʿAmr ibn Qays ibn Zāʾida ibn al-Aṣamm ibn Ahra ibn Rawāḥa al-Qurashī al-Fihrī, of Banū ʿĀmir ibn Luʾayy; and the name of his mother was ʿĀtika bint ʿAbd Allāh al-Makhzūmiyya, and he was the son of the maternal aunt of Khadīja bint Khuwaylid – embraced Islam early in Mecca. That was because he came to the Prophet ﷺ while he was conversing privately with ʿUtba ibn Rabīʿa, Abū Jahl, his uncle al-ʿAbbās, Ubayy ibn Khalaf and his brother Umayya, calling them to Islam and hoping for their belief. Ibn Umm Maktūm said: "O Messenger of Allah, teach me and instruct me from what Allah has taught you", and he kept calling out to him and repeating the call, not knowing that he was turned toward others, until dislike appeared on the face of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ at his interrupting his speech, and he said to himself: "These chiefs will say: only boys and slaves follow him." So he frowned, turned away from him, and turned to the people he had been addressing. Then Allah revealed these verses, reproaching the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. After that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would honour him whenever he saw him and say: "Welcome to the one on whose account my Lord reproached me", and would say to him: "Do you have any need?" He appointed him as his deputy over Medina twice.
He was among the first Emigrants; and it was said that he was killed as a martyr at al-Qādisiyya.
- (لعلّ):
It is a particle that governs its noun in the accusative and its khabar in the nominative, and it has meanings:
1- Expectation (tawaqquʿ): which is hoping for the desirable and fearing the undesirable, as in: (لعل الحبيب واصل) and (لعل الرقيب حاصل); and it is specific to the possible.
2- Reason (taʿlīl): as in the saying of the Exalted: (فَقُولا لَهُ قَوْلًا لَيِّناً لَعَلَّهُ يَتَذَكَّرُ أَوْ يَخْشى).
3- Interrogation: the Kufans affirmed it, and for this reason the verb is suspended (ʿulliqa) by it in, for example, the saying of the Exalted (لا تَدْرِي لَعَلَّ اللَّهَ يُحْدِثُ بَعْدَ ذلِكَ أَمْراً) (وَما يُدْرِيكَ لَعَلَّهُ يَزَّكَّى).
And its khabar is often accompanied by (أن), by analogy with (عسى), as in the verse of Mutammim ibn Nuwayra:
لعلك يوما أن تلمّ ملمة ... عليك من اللائي يدعنك أجدعا
(Perhaps one day a calamity will befall you, of those that leave you maimed.)

safi-cedvel:5-10.t:
* I'rab:
(أمّا) a particle of condition and detailing. (من) a relative in the position of nominative, a mubtadaʾ. (الفاء) links to the apodosis of أمّا. (له) attached to (تصدّى). (الواو) circumstantial (ḥāliyya). (ما) negative [Note: or an interrogative noun in the position of nominative, a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is (عليك)]. (عليك) attached to an omitted fronted khabar. (ألّا) a maṣdar particle governing the accusative, and a particle of negation..
And the interpreted maṣdar (ألّا يزّكّى..) is in the position of nominative, a postponed mubtadaʾ [Note: or in the position of genitive by an omitted preposition attached to the khabar of the interrogative ما, i.e.: "what is upon you in his not purifying himself?"].
Clause: «من استغنى ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause: «استغنى ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative (من).
And the clause: «أنت له تصدّى» is in the position of nominative, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (من).
And the clause: «تصدّى» is in the position of nominative, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (أنت).
And the clause: «ما عليك ألّا يزّكّى» is in the position of accusative, a ḥāl from the fāʿil of تصدّى.
And the clause: «يزّكّى» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the particle-type relative (أن).
8- 10 (الواو) conjunction. (أمّا من جاءك) like أمّا من استغنى. (الواو) circumstantial. (الفاء) links to the apodosis. (عنه) attached to (تلهّى).
And the clause: «من جاءك ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the resumptive clause.
And the clause: «جاءك ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative (من).
And the clause: «يسعى ... » is in the position of accusative, a ḥāl from the fāʿil of جاءك.
And the clause: «هو يخشى ... » is in the position of accusative, a ḥāl from the fāʿil of يسعى.
And the clause: «يخشى ... » is in the position of nominative, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (هو).
And the clause: «أنت عنه تلهّى» is in the position of nominative, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (من).
And the clause: «تلهّى» is in the position of nominative, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (أنت).

* Morphology:
(5) استغنى: it contains an iʿlāl by substitution; its original is استغني; the yāʾ was vowelled after a fatḥa and was changed into alif; its wazn is استفعل.
(6) تصدّى: one of the two tāʾs was deleted for lightening, and it contains an iʿlāl by substitution, its analogy being that of استغنى.
(8) يسعى: it contains an iʿlāl by substitution, like استغنى.
(9) يخشى: it contains an iʿlāl by substitution, like استغنى.
(10) تلهّى: it contains an iʿlāl by substitution, like استغنى, and the deletion of one of the two tāʾs for lightening.

safi-cedvel:11-16.t:
* I'rab:
(كلّا) a particle of rebuke and deterrence. (الفاء) conjunction. (من) a jussive-governing conditional noun in the position of nominative, a mubtadaʾ. (شاء) a past verb in the position of jussive, the protasis, and likewise the apodosis (ذكره). (في صحف) attached to a ḥāl from the third-person pronoun in (ذكره) [Note: or attached to an adjective of تذكرة ... or attached to a second khabar of إنّ, what lies between them being parenthetical]. (بأيدي) attached to (مرفوعة)..
Clause: «إنّها تذكرة ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause: «من شاء ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the resumptive clause.
And the clause: «شاء ... » is in the position of nominative, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (من) [Note: It is permissible that the khabar be the two clauses of the condition and the apodosis together].
And the clause: «ذكره ... » has no grammatical position; it is the apodosis, not accompanied by the fāʾ.

* Morphology:
(11) تذكرة: a samāʿī maṣdar of the quadriliteral ذكّر; its wazn is تفعلة with fatḥa on the tāʾ and kasra on the ʿayn.
(13) مكرّمة: feminine of مكرّم, a passive participle from the quadriliteral كرّم; its wazn is مفعّل with ḍamma on the mīm and fatḥa on the doubled ʿayn.
(15) سفرة: plural of سافر meaning "scribe", an active participle from the triliteral سفر, bāb ḍaraba; the wazn of سفرة is فعلة with three fatḥas.
(16) بررة: plural of بارّ meaning "obedient", an active participle from the triliteral برّ, bāb ḍaraba and bāb fataḥa; its wazn is فعلة like سفرة.

safi-cedvel:17-22.t:
* I'rab:
(ما) exclamatory (taʿajjubiyya), a complete indefinite meaning "something", in the position of nominative, a mubtadaʾ [Note: or it is interrogative, a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is the clause أكفره ...]. (من أيّ) attached to (خلقه). (من نطفة) attached to the second (خلقه). (الفاء) conjunction, and likewise (ثمّ) in the three places. (السبيل) a direct object of an omitted verb by way of occupation (ishtighāl), which is explained by the one mentioned after it..
Clause: «قتل الإنسان ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause: «ما أكفره ... » has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumption.
And the clause: «أكفره ... » is in the position of nominative, the khabar of the exclamatory mubtadaʾ (ما).
And the clause: «خلقه (الأولى) » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause: «خلقه (الثانية) » has no grammatical position; it is a badal from the first clause خلق.
And the clause: «قدّره ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the second clause خلقه.
And the clause: « (يسّره) السبيل» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause قدّره.
And the clause: «يسّره ... » has no grammatical position; it is explicative.
And the clause: «أماته ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the implied clause.
And the clause: «أقبره ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause أماته.
And the clause: «شاء ... » is in the position of genitive, a muḍāf ilayhi.
And the clause: «أنشره» has no grammatical position; it is the apodosis of a non-jussive-governing condition.

* Morphology:
(21) أماته: it contains an iʿlāl by substitution after the iʿlāl by making sākin; its original is أموته; the wāw was made sākin and its vowel transferred to the mīm.. then the wāw was changed into alif because what precedes it has fatḥa and it was originally vowelled; its wazn is أفعله, with fatḥa on the hamza and the ʿayn, between them a sākin fāʾ.

safi-cedvel:23-23.t:
* I'rab:
(كلّا) rebuke and deterrence from what is in man of arrogance and persistence in denying the oneness of God (tawḥīd). (لمّا) a particle of negation, inversion and jussive. (ما) a relative in the position of accusative, a direct object, the returning pronoun (ʿāʾid) being omitted, i.e.: "what He commanded him with".
Clause: «يقض ... » has no grammatical position; it is a resumption containing the meaning of reason.
And the clause: «أمره ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative (ما).

* Morphology:
(يقض): it contains an iʿlāl by deletion, to suit the jussive; its wazn is يفع.

semin-durr:2-2.t:
His saying: {أَن جَآءَهُ}: There are two aspects to it. The first: that it is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), and what makes it accusative is either «تَوَلَّى», which is the view of the Basrans, or «عَبَسَ», which is the view of the Kufans. The preferred view is the doctrine of the Basrans, because there is then no implied pronoun in the second [verb]; you have come to know the verification of this in what has preceded of the questions of tanāzuʿ (two governors competing for one word). The implied form is: because the blind man came to him, he did these two actions. The disagreement over the position of «أَنْ» after the deletion of the preposition is well known. It was also said: «أَنْ» means «إذ»; Makkī transmitted this.
Zayd ibn ʿAlī read «عَبَّس» with doubling. The majority read «أنْ» with one hamza, while Zayd ibn ʿAlī, ʿĪsā and Abū ʿImrān al-Jawnī read it with two hamzas. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It has been read «آأنْ» with two hamzas and with an alif between them; one pauses at «عَبَس وتولَّى» and then begins, with the meaning: 'Is it because the blind man came to him that he did that?'"

semin-durr:3-3.t: His saying: {لَعَلَّهُ يزكى}: The apparent view is that the expression of hope (tarajjī) is treated like interrogation in suspending (taʿlīq) [the verb], because of the sense of request common to both; for the meaning is directed at the verb of knowing taking effect over the expression of hope, the implied form being: he does not know what is hoped for from him: purification or being reminded. It was also said: the pause is at «يَدْري», and one begins with what follows, with the meaning: and what acquaints you with his affair and the outcome of his state? Then He began and said: {لَعَلَّهُ يزكى}.

semin-durr:4-4.t:
His saying: {فَتَنفَعَهُ}: ʿĀṣim read it in the accusative and the rest in the nominative. As for its accusative, it is as the response to the expression of hope (tarajjī), like His saying {فَأَطَّلِعَ} in Sūrat al-Muʾmin [verse 37]; this is a Kufan doctrine, and the discussion of it has preceded. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "[It is] in response to the wish (tamannī), because His saying «أو يَذَّكَّرُ» has the status of His saying «لعلَّه يزَّكَّى»." The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: "This is not a wish; it is only a hope." I say: he means only the wish understood from the speech, and what Abū al-Baqāʾ said indicates this: "And with the accusative as the response to the wish in meaning." Otherwise, the difference between wishing and hoping is not something Abū Muḥammad [Ibn ʿAṭiyya] would be ignorant of. Makkī said: "Whoever reads it in the accusative makes it the response of «لعلَّ» with the fāʾ, because it is not affirmative, so it resembles wishing and interrogation; but this is not known among the Basrans."
ʿĀṣim, in one transmission «[Translator's note: the text has «ورايةٍ», evidently a misprint for «روايةٍ» (transmission)]», and al-Aʿraj read «أو يَذْكُرُ» with sukūn on the dhāl and the kāf undoubled with ḍamma, the imperfect of dhakara.

semin-durr:6-6.t:
His saying: {تصدى}: The two readings, with and without doubling, have preceded / for it. Its meaning is: you present yourself [to him]. One says taṣaddā, i.e. presented himself. Its origin is taṣaddada, from al-ṣadad, which is what faces you and is in front of you; one of the identical letters was replaced by a weak letter, as in taẓannaytu and qaṣṣaytu aẓfārī, and:
4498 - تَقَضِّيَ البازِيْ. . . . . . . . . ...
(… like the swooping of the falcon …)
The poet said:
4499 - تَصَدَّى لِوَضَّاحٍ كأنَّ جَبينَه ... سِراجُ الدُّجى تُجْبَى إليه الأساوِرُ
(She presented herself to a radiant one whose brow is like the lamp of darkness, to whom bracelets are brought as tribute.)
It was also said: it is from al-ṣadā, which is the sound heard in empty places and hard bodies. It was also said: from al-ṣadā, which is thirst. The meaning is presenting oneself, and one has to strain for that if we say its origin is from sound or thirst.
Abū Jaʿfar read «تُصَدَّى» with ḍamma on the tāʾ and the ṣād undoubled, i.e. your presenting yourself urges you on towards his Islam «[Translator's note: so in the text]». One says taṣaddī al-rajul and taṣdiyatuhu. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It has been read «تُصَدَّى» with ḍamma on the tāʾ, i.e. you are made to present yourself; its meaning is: something calls you to present yourself to him, out of eagerness and keenness for his Islam."

semin-durr:7-7.t: His saying: {أَلاَّ يزكى}: a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is «عليك», i.e. his not being purified is not your responsibility.

semin-durr:8-8.t: His saying: {يسعى}: a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent of «جاءكَ», and His saying «وهو يَخْشى» is a circumstantial clause from the agent of «يَسْعى»; so it is a ḥāl from a ḥāl. Making it a second ḥāl conjoined to the first is not strong.

semin-durr:10-10.t:
His saying: {تلهى}: Its origin is tatalahhā, from lahiya yalhā bi-kadhā, i.e. he was occupied [with it]; it has nothing to do with amusement (al-lahw). The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: "It may be from it, because what is built on faʿila from roots with wāw has its wāw changed to yāʾ because of the kasra before it, as in shaqiya yashqā. If its maṣdar (verbal noun) has come with yāʾ, then it is from a root other than the root of lahw." I say: people did not make it from lahw only because it is attributed to the pronoun of the Prophet ﷺ, and it does not befit his noble rank that Allah the Exalted should attribute to him the tafaʿʿul [form] of amusement—unlike being occupied, which may issue from him at some times. Nothing other than this should be believed; the Shaykh merely slipped.
Ibn Kathīr, in the transmission of al-Bazzī from him, read «عَنْهو تَّلهَّى» with a wāw that is the extension (ṣila) of the hāʾ of the pronoun, and with doubling of the tāʾ. The origin is tatalahhā, and it was assimilated. Combining two quiescent letters was permissible because of the presence of a weak letter and assimilation. There is no parallel for this verse, namely that when the extension of the pronominal hāʾ meets another quiescent letter the extension is retained; rather, deletion is obligatory. Abū Jaʿfar read «تُلَهَّى» with ḍamma on the tāʾ, in the passive, i.e. the affairs of the chiefs distract you. Ṭalḥa read «تَتَلَهَّى» with two tāʾs, which is the origin; and from him also with one tāʾ and sukūn on the lām.

semin-durr:11-11.t: His saying: {إِنَّهَا}: The pronoun refers to the sūra or to the verses.

semin-durr:12-12.t: His saying: {ذَكَرَهُ}: The pronoun may refer to Allah the Exalted, because He is the one who sends down the reminder; or it may refer to the reminder (al-tadhkira), its pronoun being made masculine because it means remembrance (al-dhikr) and admonition.

semin-durr:13-13.t: His saying: {فَي صُحُفٍ}: a naʿt (adjective) of «تَذْكِرة»; so His saying {فَمَن شَآءَ ذَكَرَهُ} is a parenthetical clause between the adjective and what it qualifies. Similar to it is {فَمَن شَآءَ اتخذ إلى رَبِّهِ سَبِيلاً}. «في صُحُف» may also be a second khabar (predicate) of «إنَّها», the clause being parenthetical between the two khabars.

semin-durr:15-15.t:
His saying: {سَفَرَةٍ}: the plural of sāfir, which is the scribe; similar to it are kātib and kataba. And safartu between the people, asfiru, sifāra: I made peace between them. [The poet] said:
4500 - فما أَدَعُ السَّفارة بين قومي ... وما أَسْعلى بغِشٍّ إنْ مَشَيْتُ
(I do not abandon peacemaking among my people, nor do I go about with deceit when I walk [among them].)
And the woman asfarat: she uncovered her veil.

semin-durr:17-17.t: His saying: {مَآ أَكْفَرَهُ}: either an exclamation of wonder (taʿajjub), or an interrogative of wonder.

semin-durr:20-20.t: His saying: {ثُمَّ السبيل يَسَّرَهُ}: The pronoun may refer to man, with «السبيل» an adverb, i.e. He made the way easy for man, i.e. the way of good and evil, like His saying {وَهَدَيْنَاهُ النجدين} [al-Balad: 10]. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "It may be accusative as a second object of «يَسَّره», the hāʾ referring to man, i.e. He made the way easy for him, i.e. guided him to it." I say: then it must be made to include the meaning of «أَعْطى» (gave) so that it takes two objects, or the preposition is deleted, i.e. He made him ready for the way; and that is why he supplied it with his saying "guided him to it". «السبيل» may also be accusative by ishtighāl (preoccupation of the verb) by an implied verb, the pronoun referring to it, the implied form being: "then He made easy the way—He made it easy", i.e. facilitated it for people, like His saying {أعطى كُلَّ شَيءٍ خَلْقَهُ ثُمَّ هدى} [Ṭā Hā: 50]. Its like has preceded in His saying {إِنَّا هَدَيْنَاهُ السبيل} [al-Insān: 3].

semin-durr:21-21.t:
His saying: {فَأَقْبَرَهُ}: i.e. He provided him a grave. One says qabarahu when he buried him, and aqbarahu, i.e. made him such as to be buried and provided him with a grave. Al-qābir is the one who buries with his hand. Al-Aʿshā said:
4501 - لو أَسْنَدَتْ مَيْتاً إلى نَحْرِها ... عاشَ ولم يُنْقَلْ إلى قابِرِ
(If she propped a dead man against her bosom, he would live and not be carried to a burier.)

semin-durr:22-22.t: His saying: {شَآءَ}: its object is omitted, i.e. He wills his resurrection. «أَنْشَرَه» is the apodosis (jawāb) of «إذا». Shuʿayb ibn Abī Ḥamza read «نَشَره» as a triliteral; Abū al-Faḍl also transmitted it and said: "They are two dialect forms meaning bringing back to life."

semin-durr:23-23.t: His saying: {مَآ أَمَرَهُ}: «ما» is a relative noun. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "In the sense of «الذي», with the returning pronoun omitted, i.e. what He commanded him with." I say: this is questionable, in that he supplied the returning pronoun as governed by a preposition that does not govern the relative noun: "what He commanded him with". If you say: «أمرَ» takes it as object by deletion of the preposition, so I supply it as not governed by a preposition—I say: if you supply it as not governed by a preposition, you must supply it either attached or detached, and both are problematic, for the reason I set out at the beginning of al-Baqara at His saying {وَممَّا رَزَقْنَاهُمْ يُنْفِقُونَ} [al-Baqara: 3].

semin-durr:25-25.t:
His saying: {أَنَّا صَبَبْنَا المآء صَبّاً}: The Kufans read «أنَّا» with fatḥa on the hamza, without imāla of the alif; the rest read it with kasra; and al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī with fatḥa and imāla. As for the first reading, there are three aspects to it. The first: that it is a badal (substitute) for «طعامِه», so it is in the position of the genitive. Some considered this aspect problematic and rejected it, "because it is not [identical with] the first so as to be substituted for it, since food is not the pouring of water". This was answered in two ways. The first: that it is a whole-for-whole substitute with an interpretation, namely that the meaning is: let man look at Our favour in his food; so the substitution is valid. This is not clear. The second: that it is a substitute of inclusion (badal ishtimāl), in the sense that the pouring of water is a cause of bringing forth the food, so it includes it on this supposition. Makkī inclined to this and said: "Because these things include food and food is formed from them; because the meaning of «إلى طعامه» is: at how the coming-into-being of his food takes place. On this view the inclusion is of the second on the first, because the consideration is of the things from which food is formed, not of the food itself."
The second aspect: that it is on the assumption of the lām of cause, i.e. let him look, because We…; then the preposition was deleted, and the well-known disagreement about its position applies. The third aspect: that it is in the position of the nominative as the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "it is that We poured", and this has the objection mentioned before: if the pronoun refers to the food, the food is not itself the pouring, and if it refers to something else, that is not known. The answer to it is what has preceded.
As for the second reading, it is resumptive, enumerating His favours upon him. As for the third reading, it is «أنَّى», which means «كيف» (how) and contains the sense of wonder; on this reading it is one word, and on the others two words.

semin-durr:28-28.t: His saying: {وَقَضْباً}: al-qaḍb here: it was said that it is fresh dates, because they are cut (yuqḍabu) from the palm, i.e. severed. Some preferred this because of its mention after His saying «وعِنَباً», and the two are often paired. It was also said: it is fodder (al-qatt); thus the people of Mecca call it. It was also said: every vegetable cut for the children of Adam. It was also said: it is clover (al-raṭba), and al-maqāḍib is the land that grows it. Al-Rāghib said: "Al-qaḍīb is like al-qaḍb, but al-qaḍīb is used of the branches of trees and al-qaḍb of herbs. And al-qaḍb"—i.e. with fatḥa—"is cutting al-qaḍb and al-qaḍīb. From him, peace be upon him: 'When he saw cross-patterns on a garment he would cut them out (qaḍabahu).' And a sword that is qāḍib and qaḍīb, i.e. cutting; so qaḍīb here has the sense of fāʿil (active), and in the first the sense of mafʿūl (passive). And a qaḍīb she-camel is one taken from among the camels and not yet broken in. Everything that has not been refined is muqtaḍab; from it is 'improvising speech' (iqtiḍāb al-ḥadīth) for what has not been thought over and refined." Al-Khalīl said: "Al-qaḍīb: the branches of trees, so that bows / or arrows may be made from them."

semin-durr:30-30.t:
His saying: {غُلْباً}: the plural of aghlab and ghalbāʾ, like ḥumr from aḥmar and ḥamrāʾ. One says: a ghalbāʾ garden, i.e. thick with trees and intertwined; and the grass ighlawlaba, i.e. became thick. Its origin is in describing necks: one says an aghlab man and a ghalbāʾ woman, i.e. thick-necked. ʿAmr ibn Maʿdī Karib said:
4502 - يَسْعَى بها غُلْبُ الرِّقابِ كأنَّهُمْ ... بُزْلٌ كُسِيْنَ من الكُحَيْلِ جِلالا
(Thick-necked men run with it, as if they were mature camels clothed in covers of tar.)
Al-ghalaba is overpowering: that you seize and strike the thickness of his neck; this is its origin.

semin-durr:31-31.t:
His saying: {وَأَبّاً}: al-abb is for the animals what fruit is for people. It was also said: it is pasture in general. Someone said in praise of the Prophet ﷺ:
4503 - له دَعْوَةٌ مَيْمونَةٌ ريحُها الصَّبا ... بها يُنْبِتُ اللَّهُ الحَصيدةَ والأَبَّا
(He has a blessed prayer whose wind is the east wind; by it Allah makes the harvest and the pasture grow.)
It was also said: al-abb is dried fruit. Pasture was called abb because it is aimed at (yuʾammu) and sought out, and al-abb and al-amm have one meaning. [The poet] said:
4504 - جِذْمُنا قَيْسٌ ونَجْدٌ دارُنا ... ولنا الأَبُّ بِها والمَكْرَعُ
(Our root is Qays, Najd is our home, and ours in it are the pasture and the watering place.)
And abba li-kadhā, i.e. he got ready, yaʾubbu abban, abāba and abāban. And abba to his homeland, when he yearned for it, getting ready to make for it; likewise abba to his sword, i.e. got ready to draw it. Their saying «إبَّانَ ذلك» (at the time of that) is fiʿlān from it, which is the time prepared for its doing and its coming.

semin-durr:33-33.t:
His saying: {الصآخة}: the cry that deafens (taṣukhkhu) the ears, i.e. makes them deaf because of the violence of its impact. It was also said: it is taken from ṣakhkhahu with a stone, i.e. struck him with it. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Ṣakhkha to his speech is like aṣākha (he listened), so the blowing was described as al-ṣākhkha figuratively, because people listen intently to it." Ibn al-ʿArabī said: "Al-ṣākhkha is that which causes deafness, while it makes [all] hear; this is of the wonders of eloquence, like [the poet's] saying:
4505 - أصَمَّهُمْ سِرُّهُمْ أيَّامَ فُرْقَتِهمْ ... فهل سَمِعْتُمْ بسِرٍ يُوْرِث الصَّمَما
(Their secret deafened them in the days of their parting—have you ever heard of a secret that causes deafness?)
and he said:
4506 - أَصَمَّ بك النَّاعي وإنْ كانَ أَسْمَعا ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(The announcer of your death deafened [us], even though he made [us] hear …)"
The apodosis (jawāb) of «إذا» is omitted, indicated by His saying {لِكُلِّ امرىء مِّنْهُمْ يَوْمَئِذٍ شَأْنٌ يُغْنِيهِ}, i.e. the implied form is: when the deafening blast comes, everyone will be occupied with himself.

semin-durr:34-34.t: His saying: {يَوْمَ يَفِرُّ}: a badal (substitute) for «إذا». «يُغْنِيْه» cannot govern «إذا» nor «يومَ», because it is an adjective of «شَأْن», and what an adjective governs does not precede the noun it qualifies. The majority read «يُغْنيه», from al-ighnāʾ (sufficing), while Ibn Muḥayṣin, al-Zuhrī, Ibn Abī ʿAbla, Ḥumayd and Ibn al-Samayfaʿ read «يَعْنِيه» with fatḥa on the yāʾ and the undotted ʿayn, from their saying ʿanānī al-amr, i.e. the matter concerned me.

semin-durr:40-40.t:
His saying: {غَبَرَةٌ}: al-ghabara is dust, and al-qatara is a blackness like smoke. Abū ʿUbayda said: "Al-qatar in the speech of the Arabs is dust, the plural of qatara." Al-Farazdaq said:
4507 - مُتَوَّجٌ برِداءِ المُلْكِ يَتْبَعُه ... مَوْجٌ ترى فوقَه الراياتِ والقَتَرا
(Crowned with the mantle of kingship, followed by a surge above which you see banners and dust.)
I say: its conjunction to al-ghabara contains what refutes this, unless he says: since the two words differ, the conjunction is acceptable, as in [the poet's] saying:
4508 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . كَذِباً ومَيْنا
(… lying and falsehood.)
and his saying:
4509 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... . . . . . . . . . . . . النَّأْيُ والبُعْدُ
(… remoteness and distance.)
but that is contrary to the norm. The majority read «قَتَرة» with fatḥa on the tāʾ, and Ibn Abī ʿAbla gave it sukūn.

ukberi-tibyan:1-2.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (عَبَسَ وَتَوَلَّى (١) أَنْ جَاءَهُ الْأَعْمَى (٢)).
The words of the Exalted (أَنْ جَاءَهُ): i.e. «لِأَنْ جَاءَهُ» (because [the blind man] came to him).

ukberi-tibyan:4-6.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (أَوْ يَذَّكَّرُ فَتَنْفَعَهُ الذِّكْرَى (٤) أَمَّا مَنِ اسْتَغْنَى (٥) فَأَنْتَ لَهُ تَصَدَّى (٦)).
The words of the Exalted (فَتَنْفَعَهُ): in the nominative (فَتَنْفَعُهُ), conjoined to «يَذَّكَّرُ»; and in the accusative as the answer to a wish in the meaning. It is also read «تَتَصَدَّى», which is «تَتَفَعَّلُ» from «الصَّدَى», i.e. the echo [voice] — meaning: no one calls to you without your answering him. The alif may also be a substitute for a dāl, in which case it is from «الصَّدّ», i.e. the side and flank.

ukberi-tibyan:11-15.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (كَلَّا إِنَّهَا تَذْكِرَةٌ (١١) فَمَنْ شَاءَ ذَكَرَهُ (١٢) فِي صُحُفٍ مُكَرَّمَةٍ (١٣) مَرْفُوعَةٍ مُطَهَّرَةٍ (١٤) بِأَيْدِي سَفَرَةٍ (١٥)).
(إِنَّهَا): the pronoun refers to the admonition, and the pronoun in the verb [«ذَكَرَهُ»] refers to the Qurʾān.
(فِي صُحُفٍ) is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the hāʾ; it may also be a naʿt (adjective) of «تَذْكِرَةٌ», or the implied form may be «هُوَ، أَوْ هِيَ فِي صُحُفٍ» (it is in pages). Likewise «بِأَيْدِي».

ukberi-tibyan:17-17.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قُتِلَ الْإِنْسَانُ مَا أَكْفَرَهُ (١٧)).
(مَا أَكْفَرَهُ) is an exclamation of wonder (taʿajjub), or an interrogative.

ukberi-tibyan:18-19.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (مِنْ أَيِّ شَيْءٍ خَلَقَهُ (١٨) مِنْ نُطْفَةٍ خَلَقَهُ فَقَدَّرَهُ (١٩)).
(مِنْ نُطْفَةٍ) is attached (mutaʿalliq) to the second «خَلَقَ».

ukberi-tibyan:20-20.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (ثُمَّ السَّبِيلَ يَسَّرَهُ (٢٠)).
The words of the Exalted (ثُمَّ السَّبِيلَ): it is the object of an omitted verb, i.e. then He made the way easy for man. It may also be accusative as the second object of «يَسَّرَهُ», the hāʾ referring to man, i.e. He made the way easy for him, i.e. guided him to it.

ukberi-tibyan:23-23.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (كَلَّا لَمَّا يَقْضِ مَا أَمَرَهُ (٢٣)).
The words of the Exalted (مَا أَمَرَهُ): «مَا» means «الَّذِي» (that which), and the returning pronoun is omitted, i.e. «مَا أَمَرَهُ بِهِ» (what He commanded him to do). And Allah knows best.

ukberi-tibyan:24-25.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَلْيَنْظُرِ الْإِنْسَانُ إِلَى طَعَامِهِ (٢٤) أَنَّا صَبَبْنَا (٢٥)).
The words of the Exalted (أَنَّا صَبَبْنَا): with kasra (إِنَّا) as a fresh start (istiʾnāf); and with fatḥa as a badal (substitute) for «طَعَامِهِ», or on the supposition of an implied lām.

ukberi-tibyan:33-33.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَإِذَا جَاءَتِ الصَّاخَّةُ (٣٣)).
(فَإِذَا جَاءَتِ الصَّاخَّةُ) is like «جَاءَتِ الطَّامَّةُ».
It is also said that what governs «إِذَا» is the meaning of «لِكُلِّ امْرِئٍ». And Allah knows best.

zajjaj:1-2.t:
Sūrat ʿAbasa
Meccan
﷽
His saying: ﴿عَبَسَ وتَوَلّى﴾ ﴿أنْ جاءَهُ الأعْمى﴾: «أنْ» is in the position of the accusative as a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose); the meaning is: "because the blind man came to him." These verses and those after them, up to His saying ﴿فَأنْتَ عَنْهُ تَلَهّى﴾ [ʿAbasa: 10], were revealed concerning ʿAbd Allāh ibn Umm Maktūm. He had come to the Prophet ﷺ while the Prophet was calling one of the nobles of Quraysh to Islam, hoping that others would embrace Islam through his embracing it; so he, upon him be peace, was occupied with calling him and did not turn to ʿAbd Allāh ibn Umm Maktūm. So Allah commanded him not to be occupied with anyone else so as not to turn to any one of the Muslims, and said: ﴿عَبَسَ وتَوَلّى﴾ ﴿أنْ جاءَهُ الأعْمى﴾ ﴿وَما يُدْرِيكَ لَعَلَّهُ يَزَّكّى﴾ [ʿAbasa: 3] ﴿أوْ يَذَّكَّرُ فَتَنْفَعَهُ الذِّكْرى﴾ [ʿAbasa: 4]. It is also read «فَتَنْفَعُهُ الذِّكْرى». Whoever reads it in the accusative does so as the answer to «لَعَلَّ», and whoever reads it in the nominative does so by conjunction with «يَزَّكّى».

zajjaj:5-6.t: His saying: ﴿أمّا مَنِ اسْتَغْنى﴾ ﴿فَأنْتَ لَهُ تَصَدّى﴾, that is: you turn towards him. It is also read «تَصَّدّى». Whoever read ﴿تَصَدّى﴾ with the ṣād undoubled — the origin is «تَتَصَدّى», but the second tāʾ was dropped because two tāʾs came together. Whoever read «تَصَّدّى» with assimilation of the tāʾ — the meaning is also «تَتَصَدّى», except that the tāʾ was assimilated into the ṣād because the two points of articulation are close, the articulation of the tāʾ to the ṣād.

zajjaj:7-7.t: His saying: ﴿وَما عَلَيْكَ ألا يَزَّكّى﴾, that is: what blame is upon you if the one you call to Islam does not embrace Islam?!

zajjaj:10-10.t: His saying: ﴿فَأنْتَ عَنْهُ تَلَهّى﴾: its meaning is "you are occupied (away from him)". One says «لَهَيْتُ عَنِ الشَّيْءِ، ألْهى عَنْهُ» when I am occupied away from it.

zajjaj:11-11.t: His saying: ﴿كَلا إنَّها تَذْكِرَةٌ﴾: by it is meant this admonition with which Allah admonished the Prophet, upon him be peace.

zajjaj:12-12.t: ﴿فَمَن شاءَ ذَكَرَهُ﴾: the pronoun is masculine because «اَلْمَوْعِظَةُ» (admonition, feminine) and «اَلْوَعْظُ» (admonishing, masculine) are one. The meaning refers back to the bearers of the Qur'an; the meaning is: "whoever wishes to remember it remembers it." Then He, Majestic and Mighty, informed that the Book is in the Preserved Tablet with Him, saying: ﴿فِي صُحُفٍ مُكَرَّمَةٍ﴾ [ʿAbasa: 13] ﴿مَرْفُوعَةٍ مُطَهَّرَةٍ﴾ [ʿAbasa: 14] ﴿بِأيْدِي سَفَرَةٍ﴾ [ʿAbasa: 15]. «اَلسَّفَرَةُ» are the scribes, meaning the angels; the singular is «سافِرٌ», plural «سَفَرَةٌ», like «كاتِبٌ» and «كَتَبَةٌ», «كافِرٌ» and «كَفَرَةٌ». The scribes were called «سَفَرَةٌ» and the scribe «سافِرٌ» only because its meaning is that he makes a thing clear and plain. One says «أسْفَرَ الصُّبْحُ» when the dawn shines, and «سَفَرَتِ المَرْأةُ» when the woman removes the veil from her face; and from it is «سَفَرْتُ بَيْنَ القَوْمِ» ("I mediated between the people"), that is: I laid bare the heart of this one and the heart of that one, in order to reconcile them.

zajjaj:17-17.t:
His saying: ﴿قُتِلَ الإنْسانُ ما أكْفَرَهُ﴾: it may be in the form of the wording of wonder (taʿajjub), the wonder being something the children of Adam are commanded to do.
The meaning would then be like His saying: ﴿فَما أصْبَرَهم عَلى النّارِ﴾ [al-Baqara: 175], that is: you should wonder at the unbelief of man. It may also be in the sense of rebuke, its wording being the wording of a question, that is: "What has made him disbelieve?!" Then He made clear about him that by which he ought to have known that Allah is his Creator and that He is One, saying: ﴿مِن أيِّ شَيْءٍ خَلَقَهُ﴾ [ʿAbasa: 18], in the wording of a question whose meaning is to make him acknowledge (taqrīr). Then He made it clear, saying: ﴿مِن نُطْفَةٍ خَلَقَهُ فَقَدَّرَهُ﴾ [ʿAbasa: 19]; the meaning is "and He proportioned him in due form", as He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿أكَفَرْتَ بِالَّذِي خَلَقَكَ مِن تُرابٍ ثُمَّ مِن نُطْفَةٍ ثُمَّ سَوّاكَ رَجُلا﴾ [al-Kahf: 37].

zajjaj:20-20.t: His saying: ﴿ثُمَّ السَّبِيلَ يَسَّرَهُ﴾, that is: He guided him to the way, whether grateful or ungrateful.

zajjaj:21-21.t:
His saying: ﴿ثُمَّ أماتَهُ فَأقْبَرَهُ﴾: the meaning of «أقْبَرَهُ» is: He provided him with a grave in which he is hidden. One says «أقْبَرْتُ فُلانًا» — I provided him with a grave — and «قَبَرْتُ فُلانًا» — I buried him, so I am his burier (qābir). The poet said:
؎لَوْ أسْنَدَتْ مَيْتًا إلى نَحْرِها ∗∗∗ عاشَ ولَمْ يُنْقَلْ إلى قابِرِ
(Were she to lean a dead man against her bosom, he would live and not be carried off to a burier.)

zajjaj:22-22.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿ثُمَّ إذا شاءَ أنْشَرَهُ﴾: its meaning is: He resurrects him. One says «أنْشَرَ اللَّهُ المَوْتى، فَنُشِرُوا» ("Allah raised the dead, and they were raised"), and the singular is «ناشِرٌ». The poet said:
؎حَتّى يَقُولَ النّاسُ مِمّا رَأوْا ∗∗∗ يا عَجَبًا لِلْمَيِّتِ النّاشِرِ
(Until people say, at what they have seen: how wondrous, the dead man risen!)

zajjaj:24-24.t: His saying: ﴿فَلْيَنْظُرِ الإنْسانُ إلى طَعامِهِ﴾, that is: let man look at how Allah created his food and the food of all animals, which Allah made a means of their life.

zajjaj:25-25.t:
﴿أنّا صَبَبْنا الماءَ صَبًّا﴾ — it is also read «إنّا صَبَبْنا». Whoever reads «إنّا» does so as a new beginning and resumption (istiʾnāf). Whoever reads «أنّا» does so as a badal (substitute) from the food, and «إنّا» is then in the position of the genitive; the meaning is: "let man look at (the fact) that We poured down water abundantly."
«[Translator's note: in the last clause the source prints «إنّا», though the reading under discussion is «أنّا».]»

zajjaj:26-26.t: ﴿ثُمَّ شَقَقْنا الأرْضَ شَقًّا﴾, that is: with the vegetation.

zajjaj:27-27.t: ﴿فَأنْبَتْنا فِيها حَبًّا﴾: «اَلْحَبُّ» is everything that is harvested, like wheat and barley and everything having grain that is used for nourishment. «اَلْقَضْبُ» is fresh fodder (al-ruṭaba).

zajjaj:30-30.t: ﴿وَحَدائِقَ غُلْبًا﴾: «حَدائِقَ», its singular is «حَدِيقَةٌ»; they are orchards and intertwined trees. His saying ﴿غُلْبًا﴾ means: dense and large.

zajjaj:31-31.t: ﴿وَفاكِهَةً وأبًّا﴾: «اَلْأبُّ» is all the pasture that livestock graze on. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, mentioned among His signs what points to His oneness in bringing into being what nourishes all animals.

zajjaj:32-32.t: His saying: ﴿مَتاعًا لَكم ولأنْعامِكُمْ﴾: it is accusative as an emphasising maṣdar (verbal noun) of His saying "so We caused to grow in it the things that were mentioned", because His causing these things to grow has given enjoyment through them to creation, people and all animals.

zajjaj:33-33.t: His saying: ﴿فَإذا جاءَتِ الصّاخَّةُ﴾: (the blast) upon which the Resurrection takes place; it deafens (taṣikhkhu) the ears, that is, makes them deaf, so that nothing is heard except that in which there is a call to bring them to life. Then He explained at what time it comes, saying: ﴿يَوْمَ يَفِرُّ المَرْءُ مِن أخِيهِ﴾ [ʿAbasa: 34] up to His saying: ﴿لِكُلِّ امْرِئٍ مِنهم يَوْمَئِذٍ شَأْنٌ يُغْنِيهِ﴾ [ʿAbasa: 37], with dotted ghayn. It has also been read «شَأْنٌ يُعْنِيهِ», that is: an affair along with which nothing else concerns him; and likewise «يُغْنِيهِ»: being preoccupied with it, he is not able to be preoccupied with anything else. Then He made clear the states of the believers and the unbelievers. He described the states of the believers, saying: ﴿وُجُوهٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ مُسْفِرَةٌ﴾ [ʿAbasa: 38] ﴿ضاحِكَةٌ مُسْتَبْشِرَةٌ﴾ [ʿAbasa: 39] — «مُسْفِرَةٌ» means shining, having known what triumph and bliss is theirs. And He described the unbelievers and the people of the Fire, saying: ﴿وَوُجُوهٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ عَلَيْها غَبَرَةٌ﴾ [ʿAbasa: 40] ﴿تَرْهَقُها قَتَرَةٌ﴾ [ʿAbasa: 41], that is: dust over which rises a blackness like smoke. Then He made clear who the people of this state are, saying: ﴿أُولَئِكَ هُمُ الكَفَرَةُ الفَجَرَةُ﴾ [ʿAbasa: 42].
